News.title: Brit dad, 41, died on holiday in Majorca with daughter after going on late night walk then plunging from 15ft wall
News.content:
TRAGIC END Brit dad, 41, died on holiday in Majorca with daughter after going on late night walk then plunging from 15ft wall

A BRIT sadly died on holiday in Majorca while taking a late night walk and falling from a 15ft cliff, an inquest heard.

Ben Clark, 41, died instantly after he fell into a rocky area in Cala Agulla in the early hours of the morning on June 26 last year.



The dad, who lived in Andover, Hampshire, was holidaying with his daughter, Kaci Fraya, for the first time, which he was “really excited” about.

Winchester Coroner’s Court heard on Tuesday that the pair had become friends with another British woman and her aunt who they socialised around the pool with on their trip.



Area coroner Jason Pegg said the evidence showed there was clearly “some attraction” between Ben and the woman, Nicky Foers.

They decided to go for a walk together down to the beach at around 11.30pm that evening.

The coroner said it seems “slightly unclear” what caused Ben to fall from the cliff but believed alcohol probably contributed to him losing his footing.

Mr Pegg said: “All of you, particularly your dad, had consumed alcohol.



“He was not completely staggering around and out of it, but [had been] drinking nonetheless.

“There came a time on that cliff top where your dad was looking out to sea, Ms Foers looking into land, in close proximity.”

He said it was unclear what happened prior to the fall, but there was a possibility they went to hug each other and lost their balance.

Nicky told the inquest her last memory before the fall was being stood face to face, adding: “I remember seeing my feet, flip-flops coming off and just rolling and rolling and rolling.

“I’m guessing he would have given me a hug and that’s what made me stumble back.”



She said when she came round, as she believed she was unconscious, she thought Ben had not fallen and she had just slipped.

“I didn’t know if he panicked, gone to find help, I didn’t even think he’d fell,” she said.

The coroner recorded Ben’s death as an accident, after he fell down the footpath on to the beach below, causing multiple rib fractures.

These injuries led caused pulmonary haemorrhage – bleeding in the lungs – which lead to respiratory failure.

“Ben was intoxicated with alcohol which contributed to death,” he said.



The inquest, which was attended by his family, heard Ben was described as really funny, someone who adored his children and was a much-loved grandson, son, brother and father.

At the time Ben’s death was announced, tributes from his friends described him as “one of the good ones” and a “great guy”.

Kaci, in her 20s, shared a picture of the pair smiling along with a red love heart.

Clark is also believed to have been a father to a younger daughter.

Becky Paris said: “Honestly I just spent the majority of the evening blabbering on about how ‘it’s the kind of thing you read about in the newspapers, but think well it wouldn’t ever happen’ as it wasn’t real life.

“Today I am just absolutely heartbroken for you and your little family.

“No words that could make sense of it. You really were one of the good ones mate.”

News.title: Mum with VERY quirky name makes plea to Sun readers to find mystery 90s TV cop character who inspired it
News.content:
A MUM called Hollie-Popcorn Sanderson is looking for help from Sun readers to find a mystery telly cop character that inspired her quirky name.

The 31-year-old says her mum believes she named her after a female detective called “Lucy Popcorn” from a TV show in the 1990s.



But there is no trace online of the name so she is hoping someone can solve the mystery.

The mum of three has embraced her unusual name — she even has a popcorn-themed wall at her home in Uxbridge, West London.



And she has a tattoo of the cinema snack that says “fresh since 95”.

Hollie-Popcorn insists her name – which many assume is a chosen moniker – serves as an excellent icebreaker and has not held her back professionally.



The British Sign Language teacher uses “Popcorn” as her sign name.

She told The Sun: “When I was a teaching assistant, the teenagers loved it.



“I got tonnes of cards addressed to ‘Miss Popcorn’ when I left.”

She said: “As an adult I absolutely love and embrace my name.”

But she is not a fan of the stuff itself, saying: “I think popcorn’s quite dry.

“It wouldn’t be my choice and I rarely go to the cinema.”

News.title: Shocking moment motorcyclist is flung across car after smashing into bonnet – before sprinting off from crash
News.content:
THIS is the disturbing moment a biker smashed into the bonnet of a car before getting up and – in a twisted turn of events – fleeing the scene in north London.

Police were called to the scene of the crash on Moundfield Road, Stamford Hill, at 5.41pm on Sunday.



Instead of finding the victim, officers recovered “a quantity of drugs” in the aftermath of the collision.

CCTV footage showed how the bizarre incident unfolded on the quiet road.



Moments after the car stopped at a crossing, the bike smashed into its right side.

The man is flung in the air before landing on the asphalt on the other side of the vehicle.



Miraculously, he stands up – seemingly uninjured – and flees the scene on foot, abandoning his bike and one of his shoes.

Behind him, he also leaves a small package that has spilled on the asphalt.



A number of people who witnessed the crash appeared confused about why the man ran away, pointing at his direction.

Officers said they later recovered drugs from the crashed bike that was left behind.

A photo shared on X from the scene of the incident shows am officer holding a clear bag, with evidence inside.

“Enquiries are ongoing and officers are looking for the suspect who fled the scene,” a statement from the police said.

“He is described as white, with short dark hair and was wearing black trousers and a light green top.



“Anyone with information that may assist police is asked to call 101 quoting CAD 5527/16Aug.”

News.title: Net Zero has failed and made YOUR electricity more expensive – here’s my plan to cut bills by £320billion
News.content:
THE definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting a different result.

When it comes to fighting climate change, we have been doing the same thing for years — setting targets, ploughing money into government subsidies and failed schemes, while deindustrialising Britain and sending jobs to China.



We’ve all made massive sacrifices. And, in return, we’ve had steadily hotter summers and rainier winters.

If that isn’t evidence that Net Zero isn’t working, then I don’t know what is.



The targets to cut greenhouse gas emissions, set by Ed Miliband in 2008 and continued by previous Conservative governments, have driven up energy costs, weakened our industrial base and made us more and more dependent on foreign imports with higher emissions.

But they are not solving climate change. In fact, they are making the problem worse by making electricity so expensive barely anyone can afford to adopt clean technologies.



When bills are up, money is tight and people delay green upgrades and are put off buying electric cars or installing heat pumps.

We’ve become a warning to the rest of the world.

A new report, by the think tank Onward in collaboration with the Shadow Energy Secretary Claire Coutinho, says that an electricity grid that prioritised cutting bills instead of Net Zero would save consumers more than £320billion over 20 years, make Britian’s electricity a third cheaper by 2050, and still be nearly 80 per cent clean.

Unlike Labour, who are wedded to the old failing plans, or Reform, who still don’t believe climate change is happening, the Conservatives will bring common sense back to energy policy.



Andy Burnham entered No10 promising to right the wrongs of Keir Starmer.

It was suggested Burnham would approve the new licences for Rosebank and Jackdaw — the oil and gas fields awaiting approval for drilling in the North Sea.

A month later and he seems to be kicking the decision down the road because he’s worried about the “optics”. This is a shameful absence of leadership.

With Burnham pushing ahead with Miliband’s mad plan to ban all new licences, it should come as no surprise that our biggest oil company, BP, has decided to put its North Sea business up for sale.



But they are merely following in the footsteps of refinery operators, chemicals firms, ceramic manufacturers and thousands of other companies who have given up operating in Britain, unable to weather the combination of energy costs and the hostile tax and regulatory environment under Labour.

It just does not have to be like this.

We can care for our environment and move towards clean energy without scorching the earth with taxes, bans and mandates.

Net Zero is a political programme, not a law of nature.



We should preserve our countryside, encourage biodiversity, invest in flood defences and ensure Britain is resilient in the face of a changing climate.

We currently have the highest industrial energy prices in the developed world, and domestic energy prices are increasing at a rate faster than Labour can subsidise them with taxpayer handouts.

Onward’s report exposes just how much extra you are going to have to pay to get Britain to Net Zero.

We will soon be spending billions building pylons and cables, carving up the countryside in the process.

We will have to pay for expensive back up for when the wind’s not blowing. And we’ll pay even more to switch wind farms off when the wind’s blowing too hard.



This is absurdity. All of the costs simply end up on your energy bills.

All this is doing is making electricity expensive so factories shut down here, then move to China which has an exceptionally high rate of approving and building new coal plants or reactivating old ones.

That does not reduce emissions, it just changes where they come from — while costing Britain jobs, investment and prosperity.

The most important thing we can do to protect our industry, to cut bills for families, and to help the environment, is to make electricity as cheap as possible.

All of this is why my Conservative Party has pledged to scrap the carbon tax — the biggest green levy — and scrap the legally binding target for Net Zero by 2050.



That target is suffocating government in legal action by green groups, pushing up bills and strangling business with more and more reporting duties and regulations.

Together, our changes will save families £200 off their electricity bills, give a lifeline to our automotive industry, and revive oil and gas production in the North Sea and all of the jobs it supports in Aberdeen and across the United Kingdom.

This is not just about our economy and jobs, it’s about everyone’s cost of living and quality of life, it’s about common sense.

For instance, the Net Zero rules currently ban installing air conditioning in new homes.

That’s another ban that I’ll scrap, in the interests of all of us who have been suffering sleepless nights and grumpy days in this hot summer.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Onward’s report is just the latest in a bank of research and evidence that we are building to make the case for a complete change of thinking on energy.

No other party is doing this detailed work and no other party is ready to take the tough choices to get Britain working again.

News.title: Scrapping Net Zero power grid drive would leave families £540 a year better off, says Kemi Badenoch
News.content:
FAMILIES could be £540 a year better off if Britain ditches the dash for a fully Net Zero power grid, says Kemi Badenoch.

Scrapping the drive would save £320billion over 20 years, according to the Tories.



A report by the party today reveals using more nuclear and gas, and fewer renewables, would cut electricity system costs by up to almost a third by 2050.

And the electricity generated would still be nearly 80 per cent cleaner.



Tory leader Kemi Badenoch’s Shadow Energy Secretary Claire Coutinho is to present the findings of the report by think-tank Onward and energy advisers Transira Energy.

It says the price of wind and solar fail to reflect extra costs loaded on bills such as pylons, cables and back-up generation when the wind does not blow.

She will blast former Energy Secretary Ed Miliband’s Clean Power 2030 target for trying to remove carbon from electricity generation no matter the cost.

She will also accuse him of axing a full costing of renewable power which she commissioned when Energy Secretary.

She will add: “Conservatives are not in denial about climate change, it’s the Left who are in denial about the fact their climate policy is failing.”

The legally-binding target to hit Net Zero by 2050 was introduced by the Tories in 2019.



Mrs Badenoch says doing so would be impossible without bankrupting Britain.

New Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said the Tories would “tie Britain to the fossil fuel roller-coaster and keep bills higher for families”.

News.title: Three members of same family die after getting into difficulty in sea at Shoreham – as young girl fights for life
News.content:
THREE members of the same family have died and a fourth has been left fighting for her life after being swept out to sea at a beach in Shoreham.

A teenage girl and her two parents drowned after getting into difficulty in the water this afternoon – sparking a major recovery operation.



One of the girls became trapped in a fishing net during the horror, one witness said.

Sussex Police said tonight: “Tragically, despite the best efforts of paramedics, three people, a man, a woman, and a teenage girl, were sadly confirmed deceased.





“A younger girl has been taken to hospital and is in critical condition.

“We can confirm, all four people were from the same family, and their next of kin had been informed.”



They added: “At this point, we believe all four entered the water from the land for a swim, and sadly, got into difficulty.”

Emergency crews were seen carrying out CPR on three of the victims as they were dragged back to the seafront.

Police are not searching for anyone else.

An investigation has been launched to understand the full circumstances of the tragedy.



Witness Joe Chrisp, 24, said: “One of the local fishermen said it was two adults, two kids.

“One of the kids apparently got caught in a fishing net.”

Witnesses also described seeing “mayhem” unfold as the massive emergency services team swooped on the seafront.

They also said the weather today was very windy, and that the sea appeared to be choppy.



Local fishermen alerted police to Britain’s latest water tragedy after seeing a young girl in trouble shortly before 3pm.

They then saw another panicked young girl, a woman and a man also fighting against the waves.

Two helicopters, eight ambulances, lifeboat crews and the coastguard rushed to the scene shortly after the alarm was raised.

Horrified families watched on from the shoreline as a huge rescue operation swung into action.

Victoria Flint, of nearby Horsham, was there with husband Gary and their children.



She said: “We arrived at about three and soon after we heard the siren for the lifeboat.

“We watched it launch and then, about 20 minutes later, it came back. Ambulances started arriving.

“More and more of them. Then the air ambulances started.”

Resident Pete Book said: “As I neared home, a yellow air ambulance also landed.

“There were a lot of ambulances, coastguard and police vehicles converging on the area, and the coast road was closed.”



Landscaper Mr Chrisp, 24, added: “It happened when I was on my way back from work. There were loads of police and I got turned around. It’s so tragic.”

One local, who did not wish to be named, said: “It’s the first time in my 30 years living here that I’ve seen a police car drive onto the pebbles.

“It was mayhem, there were so many emergency vehicles so you knew it was something serious.”

Steve Chapman, who lives opposite the beach, said: “There were all sorts of rumours flying around, it was very upsetting.”

Shirley Pumfrey, who lives near the harbour mouth, said: “The whole road was just full of emergency services. It was horrific and quite scary to see that many.”



The RNLI said it had launched rescue boats from Shoreham Harbour at 2.51pm.

Two more followed from Brighton shortly after 3pm. A coastguard helicopter joined the search at 2.45pm along with three more rescue teams.

Aerial images showed the lifeboat returning as two air ambulances and scores of paramedics waited at the station.

Sussex Police previously said following the dramatic ordeal: “Emergency services are currently responding to reports of four people in difficulty in the water close to Shoreham Fort.

“A section of the A259 in Shoreham has been closed as the incident remains ongoing, and we’re urging the public to stay clear of the area in the meantime.”



Today’s horror is the latest in a recent spate of water tragedies across the country.

It comes just weeks after a seven-year-old boy drowned alongside his teenage cousin and her mum at the beach on a family holiday.

Musa Ahmed, seven, died in hospital six days after getting into difficulty in the water in West Mersea, Essex, on July 22.

His cousin Sameeha Rahman, 15, and her mother Shelina Rahman, 41, also died in the horror.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And just yesterday, the body of a 12-year-old boy was sadly pulled from a river following a search by divers.



Emergency crews were called to reports of a person in the water near Hackney Marshes, East London, shortly after 6pm on Saturday.

News.title: BA cabin worker ‘sexually assaulted colleague by rubbing her bum while pleasuring himself after vodka binge’
News.content:
BA 'SEX ATTACK' RAP BA cabin worker ‘sexually assaulted colleague by rubbing her bum while pleasuring himself after vodka binge’

A BRITISH Airways cabin worker sexually assaulted a colleague on a boozy stop-over, a court heard.

Ryan Lim, 31, is accused of pleasuring himself while rubbing the stewardess’s bottom as she slept in a hotel bed with him and another male.



She says she was woken by Lim’s “sexual moaning” before seeing his hand moving up and down in a bedroom mirror.

The crew went on a drinking spree after arriving in Rio de Janeiro from London and captain James Hewitt bought a bottle of vodka in a club around midnight.



Speaking at Isleworth crown court, the alleged victim said she does not remember how she came to be in her male colleague’s hotel room with him and Lim — but was woken up by the assault.

She said: “As I woke up, I felt my bum being touched.



“I heard sexual moaning from right beside me.

“He was rubbing my bum. I was facing a mirror, a sliding door. I saw movements of the bedsheets, like a hand movement up and down.”



She then got out of bed and went to the bathroom where she threw up and heard her two male colleagues speaking before going to confront Lim. She added: “He became a bit frantic — he could see I was very uncomfortable.

“He said, ‘What happens in this room stays in this room’.”

The alleged assault was reported to Brazilian police and captain Hewitt. Two BA flights were cancelled as a result.

She claimed she was about “five-out-of-ten” drunk.

Lily Hayes, prosecuting, said: “[The victim] says that at no point did she consent to be sexually touched.”



Sophia Kerridge, defending, said yesterday: “You woke up in a room with two boys, you were coming in and out of sleep when you noticed something that could be sexual activity.

“At the time you were not sure what you had experienced was something more innocent. I suggest to you it didn’t happen because you would have been in a rush to leave that room.”

Lim, of Sunderland, denies sexual assault. Trial continues.

News.title: London fire live: Bermondsey blaze involves 50 tonnes of waste as trains blocked
News.content:
A massive fire has erupted at a waste facility in Deptford/Bermondsey in south-east London, with people sharing footage online of huge flames and plumes of smoke rising over the skyline

Huge flames and clouds of smoke can be seen coming from a major fire in south-east London on Tuesday evening.

The London Fire Brigade said 15 fire engines and around 100 firefighters are responding to a fire at a waste facility on Landman Way in Deptford/Bermondsey. Local residents have been urged to keep windows and doors closed.

National Rail says it is expecting disruption at London Bridge until the end of the day due to the fire, with services possibly "cancelled, delayed or revised".

News.title: UK weather maps show exact time violent thunderstorms and rain to batter nation
News.content:
UK weather maps show exact time violent thunderstorms and rain to batter nation

New weather forecast maps show a deluge day incoming for most of the UK this week, with heavy rain, some hail, and a massive band of thunder streaking across every home nation

View 4 Images Heavy rain will douse parched parts of the country this Thursday (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Dramatic new weather maps capture the exact date and time a series of violent thunderstorms will smash Britain - with the Met Office raising the potential threat of flash flooding.

‌



More than half of the country is in drought but welcome rain is on the horizon with the rain. Thunderstorms and downpours have already swept through Scotland and Northern Ireland, and will move south into England and Wales as the week progresses.

‌



The heaviest of which, forecasters say, will arrive on Thursday. According to the latest weather maps, some of the most drought-hardened areas will be hit hard just as people prepare to leave the office for their commutes home. It will be colder than the last few days too, with lows of 12C forecast across northern England.

‌



Met Office names areas facing lightning and hail on Wednesday – 33 counties at risk READ MORE :

View 4 Images Forecasts show thunder and lightning moving south throughout Thursday (Image: Ventusky)

The maps from Netweather.tv and Ventusky capture the rain as it arrives over the UK on Thursday, August 20, in the afternoon, and into the evening. The latter service shows the first drops arriving over the southeast after rotating in from Northern Ireland and Scotland, tipping out up to 6mm of water per hour from the northwest coast.

The initial wave will hit areas like Aberystwyth in Wales and both Liverpool and Blackpool in northern England, starting from around 1am.

‌



The system will continue to move inland from there, with maps showing forks of lightning streaking out alongside some potential hail. Rain will initially centre itself around Yorkshire, with Leeds, Middlesborough and Scarborough all taking the brunt of still heavy 6mm to 8mm of rain per hour.

View 4 Images Rain will pound the country heavily when it arrives this week (Image: Netweather.tv)

The same system will move south throughout the day until landing in the Midlands and East of England at Birmingham and Norwich by around 4pm.

‌



As those areas see heavier raingall at the time, slightly lighter rainfall and showers will arrive over London and most of southern England, aside from distant parts of the southwest coast like Devon and Cornwall. Those same areas will come within the heavier rain by around 7pm, and it will remain there until 10pm.

All the while, the Netweather maps show the country remaining comparatively warm, with the UK's capital and the vast majority of the southeast wrapped in 22C highs.

View 4 Images As the rain falls, temperatures will remain comparatively high (Image: Netweather.tv)

Article continues below

Areas further north, including those where the rain is set to hit first, will be fresh, with highs hitting between 13C and 17C at a maximum. The forecast for the day is the start of a wetter trend, according to the Met Office, which predicts that, between August 23 and September 1, "most places" will continue to see some showers.

The forecast states: "This period is likely to start largely dry and settled across the UK, as a ridge of high pressure sets in. A few showers are likely in the far north and possibly the far southeast though. Conditions look like turning increasingly unsettled through next week, as low pressure gradually becomes dominant, squeezing the ridge off to the northeast.

"Most places are likely to see some rain or showers, particularly during the second half of next week, and these may be heavy with a risk of hail and thunder. It may become breezy if not windy at times too. Temperatures are likely to be near or a little below normal overall, with some chilly nights at first, but brief warm, humid spells are possible at times, especially in the south."

News.title: Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36: Ex Brian Hickerson at scene when she died as mum breaks silence
News.content:
Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36, with the initial investigation from police finding there was 'no foul play' and autopsy results confirming 'no signs of trauma'

US actress Hayden Panettiere, who was best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. Her death was confirmed by her representatives and followed by a statement.

The statement from her father, Skip, read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”

Meanwhile, her mother spoke the first time on Tuesday, firing shorts at ex Brian Hickerson. She said: "I think Hayden was an amazingly talented person in so many departments and I think young people who grow up in the entertainment industry -- it is a struggle and it's a very challenging industry and it's not unusual for them to sadly find the wrong path."

She also added: "This person in her life that we have been trying to get rid of for quite some time was with her at her death, and that was Brian Hickerson."

The Coroner's office confirmed that Hayden's autopsy showed 'no signs of trauma' at the time of her death. It had been reported that the police were responding to a call about a suspected "cardiac arrest". A police report later revealed that both her ex Hickerson and his brother Zach were at the scene at the time of her death.

911 audio footage also heard dispatchers discuss a suspected overdose. Both Narcan and Epinephrine were reportedly brought to the scene by emergency services Panettiere's cause of death has not been announced at this time.

A preliminary police investigation has confirmed there were no signs of "foul play or suspicious circumstances" when they arrived at her home after a 911 emergency call from an acquaintance of Panettiere's.

News.title: Shoreham emergency live: Three family members dead after being pulled from sea
News.content:
Three people from the same family died after being pulled from the water in Shoreham-by-Sea in West Sussex on Tuesday - coastguard helicopters, ambulances and police were called to the scene

Shoreham emergency live: Three family members dead after being pulled from sea

Three people from the same family - a man, a woman and a teenage girl - died after getting into trouble in water off Shoreham-by-Sea on Tuesday.

A younger girl from the same family is in a critical condition in hospital, Sussex Police said.

Coastguard helicopters, ambulances and police were scrambled to the coastal town in West Sussex following reports that four people were in trouble in the water.

The RNLI said lifeboat crews were launched from Shoreham at about 2.50pm on Tuesday afternoon. Two other lifeboats were also launched from the Brighton lifeboat station shortly after 3pm.

News.title: Drunk Jet2 passenger 'ruined holidays' of 300 passengers with what he said to crew
News.content:
Drunk Jet2 passenger 'ruined holidays' of 300 passengers with what he said to crew

Jason Mulhern, 57, forced a Jet2 flight to Dalaman in Turkey to be cancelled at Manchester Airport after he became abusive to cabin crew during a drunken tirade, a court heard

View 2 Images Jason Mulhern, 57, was abusive towards cabin crew, the court heard (Image: Manchester Evening News)

A Jet2 passenger launched a drunken tirade which forced the flight with 300 passengers to be cancelled.

‌



Jason Mulhern, 57, and his wife were on a plane at Manchester Airport heading to Dalaman in Turkey on June 22, 2024, when he became abusive.

‌



Manchester Crown Court was told that first the defendant's wife made a comment about a fellow passenger's accent before he joined in and began 'shouting', reports Manchester Evening News.

‌



Cabin staff then spoke to them both and they were told they would not be served alcohol, leading Mulhern, of Trafford, to become 'aggressive, defensive and angry', said the prosecution.

View 2 Images Mulhern's behaviour led to a flight being cancelled (Image: Manchester Evening News)

Met Office names areas facing lightning and hail on Wednesday – 33 counties at risk READ MORE :

He told staff they were 'out of order', that he and his wife were 'on their holidays' and wanted to 'booze up'. They were spoken to again, with a warning from the captain that they would be removed if they continued, after which they 'disgruntledly' accepted the situation.

‌



However, as the plane began to taxi to the runway, Mulhern shouted at one of the crew that she was a 'f***ing Nazi and a c***'. He added that 'he was an adult and could do as he wished'.

Betsy Hindle, prosecuting, said that the 20-year-old crew member felt so uncomfortable and intimidated that she moved seats while the plane was taxiing. "The defendant was saying: 'You can't call anyone a c*** these days, even when they are being one. If I want to call you a c***, I will'. He also said all the crew were Nazis," Ms Hindle said.

The court heard the captain was informed, who then made the decision to have Mulhern and his partner removed, to the applause from other passengers. As a result, the flight was abandoned and had to return to the stand, and the police were called. The court heard that the flight had already been delayed for two hours.

‌



Mulhern was spoken to by officers on board, and was described as slurring his words and speaking over them. As they explained that he had committed an offence, he replied: "Oh f*** off", before telling them: "I can say whatever I want, it's a free county. If I think you're a Nazi, I'll say it."

"As a result of this, the aircraft was significantly delayed and cancelled altogether due to restrictions on safe flying hours. Three hundred passengers had to disembark and decontrol through security. Accommodation and meals had to be sought for those on the flight. Also 300 passengers in Turkey were affected, who were due to return to Manchester on that same plane," Ms Hindle told the court.

The court heard that various statements were taken from passengers. One described Mulhern as 'obviously drunk', and being 'verbally abusive'. Another said they heard him say to staff: "I don't understand why I can't have a drink like a f***ing adult'.

‌



Ms Hindle said Jet2 have said they will be seeing a civil claim to the amount of £44,710, which includes costs of hotels and delays.

Lisa Judge, defending, urged the court to consider the case to be at the 'lowest level of culpability' due to the lack of violence. She accepted that Mulhern and his wife had been drinking prior to the flight, and said the flight had already been delayed.

"This was the use of language only," she said. She said his character references showed him to be an important person in his team, who was 'responsible and mature'. She also said his previous service in the Armed Forces had left him 'self-medicating' with alcohol.

‌



"Nobody was forcing you to drink. There was no need to drink, that was a choice you took," Judge Elizabeth Nicholls said. "Your conduct caused the plane to be delayed again. Your conduct alone was responsible for the loss of that day's flight. A flight that everyone's holidays had to be deferred, everyone had to make alternative arrangements, everyone had to be put up in hotels.

"You ruined or potentially ruined every other person's holiday who boarded that flight. That was the impact of your single behaviour."

Judge Nicholls told Mulhern, who was supported by his wife in the public gallery: "What you did was quite frankly despicable. It caused chaos and distress to a large number of people. I hope you now understand the consequences of your behaviour."

Article continues below

Mulhern, of Jewel Close, Urmston, was handed eight months imprisonment suspended for 18 months. He must also complete five days of rehabilitation activity requirements, a 120-day alcohol abstinence order and 300 hours unpaid work, and must pay £500 in court costs. The court heard he also has a lifelong ban from travelling with Jet2.

News.title: Burnham's homelessness mission can't come soon enough — Victoria’s story shows why
News.content:
She might have been a rough sleeper, but Victoria was often too scared to catch any shut-eye.

The 31-year-old said: "The minute men realised I was vulnerable and homeless, they would begin to offer me money to do things with them. I felt unsupported, alone and suicidal.”

Victoria’s harrowing experience – shared with the Single Homeless Project [SHP], which helped her get back on her feet – lays bare the hardship of those experiencing rough sleeping. And, in particular, it shines a light on the vulnerability of women who have no place to call home.

Andy Burnham has a mountain to climb if he is to truly tackle an issue which successive governments have struggled to grapple with. The PM is pledging what the government calls “immediate action to offer everyone who needs it a route off the streets by Christmas”.

‌



Hidden homeless scandal as nearly double number of women sleep rough than official stats READ MORE :

Remarkable survival story of elderly gent who Prince William hugged at homeless charity READ MORE :

View 3 Images Andy Burnham pledged to end the blight of rough sleeping (Image: Paul Marriott/Shutterstock)

The move is backed by an additional £102million, on top of the £340million funding unveiled last month. It follows Burnham’s pledge, in his first speech after taking up post in Number 10, to end the blight of rough sleeping. His intervention is certainly needed. The number of rough sleepers in England in autumn last year was estimated to be 4,793 – up 3% year-on-year.

Francesca Albanese, director of policy and social change at Crisis, has worked in the sector for nearly two decades but warned: “Things have definitely got worse in the last ten years.”

She added: “When we saw welfare reform and that squeeze on housing benefit and other welfare services, it’s had a direct hit… Under normal circumstances if you have enough money to pay rent, you’re not pushed onto the streets. I’d definitely seen that lack of affordable housing really driving things and meaning that people are coming to us.”

‌



The hidden homeless: Mirror investigates England's rough sleeping scandal

She cited an increase in older people coming to the charity’s services, as well as working individuals. Ms Albanese explained “We have had rising levels of rough sleeping over many years. One of the biggest drivers of that is a lack of housing.” She added: “The announcement at the moment is about that emergency provision, so it’s about how do you get people off the streets quickly.

“And that’s really important. Having some form of accommodation in an emergency means that people can get linked into other services. But it’s got to then have move on accommodation so making sure you’ve got the homes there.”

Keir Starmer’s government announced a decade-long £39billion social and affordable homes programme. Ms Albanese said: “We’ve got to make sure that that’s unlocked quickly."

‌



For Shelter’s policy manager, Deborah Garvie, housing is key. She said: “The biggest challenge, as with all forms of homelessness, is the dire shortage of social rent homes. So that can mean even where people are helped off the street into emergency or temporary accommodation then they’re unable to move on… into a home of their own.”

Another pertinent point is an understanding of the scale of the issue. A Mirror investigation in 2024 revealed how a charity census identified over a thousand women sleeping rough – nearly twice as many as government figures had earlier shown.

View 3 Images Lucy Campbell, assistant director at the Single Homeless Project, says: 'We need to be identifying people rough sleeping in different ways.'

Lucy Campbell, assistant director at charity SHP, said: “What we really want to push is that local authorities who are going to be receiving these funds and putting strategies in place to get people off the streets aren’t just going to be operating it again on that kind of government snapshot count definition of what rough sleeping is.

‌



“We need to be identifying people rough sleeping in different ways. We need to be undertaking gender-informed outreach and building in no wrong door approaches between different services to actually identify the women in the first place. Because we’re not likely to see them bedded down on the high street. They’re not doing that because of fear of violence and that means they are at risk of being missed by any new initiatives that are put in place to get people off the streets.”

Burnham’s not the first PM to talk big on homelessness. Campaigner Kerri Douglas, who has experienced rough sleeping, said: “We’ve heard this all before though with these pledges of lots of money but nothing ever gets done, does it? So it’ll be nice to see how this gets spent this time round.”

Yet she does have some optimism things might be different. “I do have a bit of hope,” the 42-year-old said. “And I do think that he’s going to make a difference but I think he’s got high expectations in little timescales to be doing it.”

For those out on the streets tonight, help cannot come soon enough.

News.title: Villagers left without water for DAYS spell 'help us' with empty bottles in desperate plea to South East Water
News.content:
Villagers left without water for DAYS spell 'help us' with empty bottles in desperate plea to South East Water

South East Water has been widely criticised for its failure to handle water outages across Kent, with the August supply issues being just the latest seen this year

View 8 Images Residents of a Kent village staged a water bottle protest after they were left without water (Image: Nicola Stanway /PA Wire)

Furious locals living in a water-starved village staged a desperate water bottle protest against South East Water after they were left without a supply.

‌



The firm, one of eight water companies across England and Wales currently included in hosepipe ban restrictions, has warned its customers in Kent that drinking storage tanks are "critically low", and told them to only turn on the taps for "essential" purposes.

‌



But the firm has come under fire after supply issues left thousands of people without access to even those critical supplies, leaving locals in one Kent town, Benenden, with no recourse but to put together an eye-catching protest.

‌



Residents, who said South East Water's handling of the situation was "shocking", spelled out the words "help us" with their depleted water bottles.

View 8 Images Water bottles have been handed out to Kent residents (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

‌



Around 7,400 properties in Herne Bay, Rough Common and Blean in Kent had their water supplies restored as of Tuesday morning, but 400 were still struggling with low pressure, or any water access at all. Residents staged their protest on Monday, where they met out on the Benenden village green - turned straw yellow by the drought.

The group of between 60 to 70 people, who had collected all the plastic water bottles they had been using, laid them out to spell their plea on the parched ground.

One Benenden resident, Nicola Stanway, told the Press Association that everyone in the village wants to be heard and have a voice. She said she had retreated to the local pub, the Bull at Benenden, after being left without water for five days.

‌



View 8 Images Nicola Stanway went to the pub after being left without water since Thursday (Image: Anahita Hossein-Pour/PA Wire)

Nicola, 41, an estate agent, said: “This morning I haven’t received any deliveries of water so been reliant on coming here and using Lucy’s (pub landlord) water.

“But we have seen lots of houses around here that are empty with bottled water, it’s ridiculously distributed, it’s not been well planned or orchestrated at all.” Nicola added that South East Water's handling of the situation was "disappointing", adding: "It’s frustrating, the amount of excuses, every couple of days it’s something different.”

‌



Pub owner Lucy Barron-Reid said the protest of around 60 to 70 people was to prove a point how much people use plastic bottled water for basic washes, going to the toilet, cooking, cleaning and looking after animals.

View 8 Images SEW is among water companies included on the hosepipe ban list (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

For her business, she said: “Apart from Covid this is the hardest thing we have had to deal with. Over the last few years we have had sporadic water outages and this year has become really severe, which has been extremely difficult to run a business.”

‌



She said they made the decision to remain open since losing water last Thursday to avoid joining the statistics of pubs that close down.

The pub landlady of 22 years said the handling from South East Water is “absolutely shocking” and as a business in the outages they have to buy their own water from a different company. “But our community has stepped in,” the 56-year-old said, adding it is getting to the point they have not got water either.

View 8 Images Pub landlady Lucy Barron-Reid said SEW's handling of the situation was 'shocking' (Image: Anahita Hossein-Pour/PA Wire)

‌



“Everyone’s a bit stuffed. It’s just really exhausting mentally and physically,” she said. “It really is very scary, a couple of times on Saturday I got very upset and very tearful, I don’t want to do this anymore.”

The Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) said another disruption for South East Water (SEW) customers was “simply not good enough”.

A Defra spokesperson said: “South East Water needs to go further and faster to reduce leaks and follow their drought plans to ensure supplies are not disrupted in even the driest of weather. Their new leadership must now deliver a step change in performance, where customers’ needs are prioritised and there is a stop to supply outages.”

‌



View 8 Images Local MP Katie Lam hsa furiously railed against SEW (Image: PA)

It is the latest in a string of incidents SEW customers have faced, and Weald of Kent MP Katie Lam, whose constituency includes the areas still impacted by the issues, said outages have become “depressingly common”.

She said the outages were "simply not good enough", adding: “People rightly expect that when they turn on the tap, water comes out. They should not have to plan their lives around the latest South East Water outage. South East Water needs fundamental transformation — the new leadership team recognise this, and they will need to move fast to achieve the reliable service people rightly demand.”

‌



In July, 7,000 homes in the Tunbridge Wells area had supply issues because of a failure at a treatment works. In Benenden, bottled water was left outside houses while a South East Water van was seen driving through the village.

View 8 Images Residents spelled out their sign using bottles handed out as their taps ran dry (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA Wire)

SEW was ordered to pay £30.5 million in July after investigations by industry watchdog Ofwat following previous supply interruptions affecting hundreds of thousands of households across Kent and Sussex.

‌



Ofwat said the redress package concluded three investigations into the supplier and includes a previously proposed £22 million fine for water supply failures between 2020 and 2023, which impacted more than 286,000 people. The regulator launched a second probe at the start of this year after more supply interruptions in Tunbridge Wells and across Kent and Sussex between November and January, which left up to 70,000 homes without water.

“After years of failure, we have taken swift action to hold water companies to account,” the Defra spokesperson added.

View 8 Images Vast parts of the country have been left depleted of water (Image: Getty Images)

Article continues below

“We have banned unfair water boss bonuses and will establish a new, single regulator with greater powers to drive transparency, helping to rebuild customer trust and protect the environment.” SEW said on Tuesday bottled water stations, including at the Weald Sports Centre in Cranbrook and Sturry Road Park and Ride in Canterbury would be open until 10pm for customers affected by the latest incident.

A spokesperson said staff and contractors had been subject to abuse in recent days. The spokesperson said: “Whilst we understand the frustrations due to the current disruption, our team is working to restore supplies and deliver water to customers. We do not tolerate any abuse towards our staff and the safety of our staff and contractors is paramount.”

News.title: Inside Sophie and Prince Edward's low-key summer as they mark family turning point
News.content:
Inside Sophie and Prince Edward's low-key summer as they mark family turning point

EXCLUSIVE: Her royal duties take her up and down the UK and to the four corners of the world - but Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh, has been able to enjoy some downtime of late

View 7 Images Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

She is one of the hardest-working royals, carrying out duties up and down the country as well as in some of the world ’s most far-flung places.

‌



So Sophie, the Duchess of Edinburgh, has no doubt relished some downtime this summer alongside husband Prince Edward and their children, Lady Louise Windsor and James, the Earl of Wessex.

‌



The Duchess, who has recently chopped her blonde hair into a sleek bob, has had a busy schedule of late, juggling a royal tour to Portugal with making several appearances at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow alongside her husband and watching on proudly as daughter Lady Louise graduated from the University of St Andrews.

‌



Lady Louise Windsor joined by boyfriend as dad Edward presents Duke of Edinburgh award in Palace celebration READ MORE :

Sophie Duchess of Edinburgh debuts dramatically shorter hair do after big chop READ MORE :

View 7 Images Sophie with husband, Prince Edward (Image: Steve Welsh/PA Wire)

As the royal calendar has entered August, Sophie has still kept up with a string of engagements, including showing off her impressive skiing skills at the Snow Centre in Hemel Hempstead where she visited the Armed Forces Para-Snowsport Team (AFPST), to mark the announcement that she has been made their royal patron.

However, the quieter period has also allowed her time off in recent weeks, and royal expert Jennie Bond tells the Mirror that instead of any lavish luxury trips to exotic locations, Sophie and the rest of the Edinburghs will have spent their time in a much more down-to-earth fashion.

‌



The former BBC royal correspondent explained: “The Edinburghs tend to spend part of the summer at Sandringham, where they stay at Wood Farm - recently used on a temporary basis by Andrew as the first stop on his exile. It’s a fairly modest farmhouse where the late Duke of Edinburgh spent much of the final years of his life.

“Like the rest of the family, they’re all pretty keen on the great outdoors, so they’ll probably head to the beach when it’s not too crowded or hit the tennis courts when it’s not too hot.

View 7 Images The Duchess on a recent trip to Lisbon (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

‌



“The family enjoy living quite modestly. Bagshot Park is enormous and, as James and Louise become more independent, I wouldn’t be surprised if the Edinburghs down-sized. And they don’t look for outlandish luxury when they go on holiday. They have sometimes been to Corfu in the summer, the birthplace, of course, of Edward’s father, Prince Philip.

“And they’ve also been known to head to the West Country to catch up with old friends. There are some extremely peaceful little spots where they can go almost unnoticed.”

But regardless of where they have been holidaying this summer, Jennie believes that Sophie, Edward and the children spending quality time together is what is most important.

‌



She added: "I think one of the secrets of their happy marriage is that they have always been and remain the very best of friends. They have supported one another through some very tricky times. But all of that just seems to have made them stronger, and it’s lovely to see them so happy in their long marriage."

However, one place Sophie and Edward are almost guaranteed to visit this month is Balmoral, for the huge Royal Family get-together.

View 7 Images The Duke and Duchess at the recent Royal Windsor Flower Show (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

‌



Like his mother before him, the King spends part of August and September on the 50,000-acre Scottish Highlands estate, welcoming various relatives for a short stay while he is in residence - with the Edinburghs almost always among them.

There, the family has endless options of enjoying long walks, fishing trips, horse rides and barbecues as the opportunity to catch up with other family members.

Before finding love with Sophie, Edward dated West End star Ruthie Henshall, who recently lifted the lid on what the Balmoral summer holiday is like, revealing how the royals love cookouts and do all their own cooking and cleaning after barbecues and picnics.

‌



And since her wedding to Edward and becoming a fully-fledged member of the Royal Family, Sophie has seemingly grown to love spending time at the Highlands retreat, especially with the late Queen and Prince Philip.

View 7 Images The Duchess of Edinburgh takes to the slopes at the Snow Centre in Hemel Hempstead (Image: Aaron Chown/PA Wire)

She shared a tight bond with both of her in-laws, and when the late Duke of Edinburgh died in 2021, Sophie shared a beautiful family photo she took of them relaxing at the Coyles of Muick near Balmoral in 2003.

‌



And her popularity within the Firm seems to extend to the younger members of the family too - with Sophie getting on famously with the Princess of Wales.

The pair are often seen chatting away and giggling at royal events, with her and Prince William said to appreciate her no-fuss attitude and admire the way she has raised her two children.

This was proved earlier this month when Sophie and Edward joined William, Kate and their children Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis to watch cycling at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, with them all greeting each other with kisses and cuddles.

‌



And Jennie added: “Because Edward is 16 years younger than his brother, the King, he and Sophie straddle the generations, and have a great rapport with them all.

View 7 Images Sophie with daughter, Lady Louise Windsor (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

“We’ve often seen how affectionate Sophie is with Charles, and also how well she gets on with William and Catherine. It’s hard sometimes to remember that she is actually their aunt by marriage, as she seems far more like an older sister.

‌



“And Edward obviously has a great relationship with both them, and their children, too. With their own offspring now young adults, Edward and Sophie probably get a nostalgic kick out of hanging out with George, Charlotte and Louis. And there’s plenty for them to join in with at Balmoral: the hiking, fishing, riding and, of course, the barbecues.”

This summer will also mark somewhat of a turning point for the Edinburghs when it comes to their children. Just last week their youngest son James, 18, received his A-level results, with Buckingham Palace announcing he would be off to university in September.

He will study for a rural land and property management degree at the Royal Agricultural University in Gloucestershire. His grades and the subjects he studied at the private Radley College in Oxfordshire were not disclosed.

‌



While their older daughter, Lady Louise, recently announced she is taking a gap year, which will be a mix of working, volunteering, and travelling before looking at her future career options.

View 7 Images Sophie shares a close bond with the Princess of Wales (Image: Getty Images)

Last month, she graduated from the University of St Andrews with a degree in English and international relations, with her graduation ceremony attended by her proud parents, who released a charming photo of their daughter in her cap and gown.

‌



She also had a sweet moment with her father earlier this summer, when he personally presented her with her gold Duke of Edinburgh award during a special ceremony at the Palace of Holyroodhouse in Edinburgh watched on by her proud mum.

Edward told his daughter: It’s all a bit staged, but it’s just to prove that you actually did get it.” As he gave her the certificate for her achievement, he told her: "Many congratulations and very well done."

And Jennie added: “This year Edward and Sophie’s son, James, has been helping out on the farm at Sandringham, driving tractors for the harvest.

‌



“He is off to university as A-Level results were up to scratch, so this summer might seem rather special for them all. And Louise has been competing in a carriage driving competition at Sandringham; she’s on a gap year after finishing at St Andrews.

“With their children now young adults, they have more time for each other and for their royal duties. Edward and Sophie have made it clear that they want their children to decide on their future.

Article continues below

“Sophie has said she has brought them up with the expectation of earning a living outside the royal family. The couple deliberately decided against making Louise and James HRHs or Princess and Prince.

“At 18 they had the choice to take up the titles if they wanted, but neither has yet done so. And that means that they have more freedom to lead ‘normal’ lives and pursue their own careers.”

News.title: Three dead after family get into difficulty in sea
News.content:
A spokesperson for Air Ambulance Charity Kent Surrey Sussex said both of its helicopters and critical care team had been sent to the scene as part of the response, and Shoreham RNLI said its lifeboat had beencalled out at 15:00 BST.

South East Coast Ambulance Service (Secamb) said it had been called to "reports of four people in need of medical attention".

A section of the A259 â a main commuter road which runs through Brighton, Shoreham and Worthing â was closed.

BBC reporter Callum French said despite warm weather, sea conditions had been "pretty rough" because of high winds, describing the response as "the biggest turnout [of emergency services] I have seen".

Witnesses described seeing large numbers of emergency vehicles and helicopters arriving at the seafront.

Resident Shirley Pumfrey said: "I have never seen them do that. The whole road was just full of emergency services.

"It was horrific and quite scary to see that many."

Steve Chapman, who lives opposite the beach, said he couldn't get into his road because it was cordoned off.

"There were all sorts of rumours flying around, it was very upsetting," he said.

Another resident, Pete Book, said he was walking home from the pub when he saw ambulances, coastguard crews and helicopters converging on the area.

Shelley Ayres, who also lives opposite the beach at Shoreham, said: "The sea has been very calm for months and months, but today it has got a lot rougher."

Tom Rutland, East Worthing and Shoreham MP, earlier urged people to stay away from the area while emergency services dealt with the incident.

After news emerged of the deaths, he said his thoughts were with the family and friends of those who had died and he added: "I know the whole community here in Shoreham will be hoping and praying for the recovery of the young girl, external receiving medical treatment in hospital."

Shoreham Port said it was working with multiple agencies and also urged the public to avoid the area.

News.title: 'Everyone in for Christmas' - Burnham unveils rough sleeping plan
News.content:
Burnham said: "No-one should have to bed down in a doorway or outside a station. But we've seen it for so long that it feels like Westminster has started to accept it. I won't accept it."

The prime minister said he wanted to build on the success of Everyone In, a Covid pandemic-era scheme that saw thousands of rough sleepers housed in hotels and temporary accommodation.

About 37,000 people were helped by the scheme following its launch in March 2020. The charity Shelter found that about a quarter of them had found settled accommodation, in the form of housing lasting at least six months., external

The announcement comes with an additional Â£102m in new funding, taking Burnham's total commitment to tackling rough sleeping to Â£442m since becoming prime minister. The money is said to be "fully funded" within the Ministry of Housing's budget.

As well as providing immediate support get people off the streets, the funding is also designed to deliver over 1,000 homes over the next three years to provide rough sleepers with permanent accommodation. The funding will also provide "intensive wraparound support," typically psychiatric and drug and alcohol services to help people rebuild their lives.

Burnham says he will organise a special conference in the autumn, inviting business, charities and faith groups to outline how they can help tackle the problem. Councils and mayors will play a leading role in devising local solutions with the areas with the biggest problem receiving the most support.

Jasmine Basran, head of policy at Crisis, said the charity welcomed the announcement and believed an end to rough sleeping was possible.

"What we also want to see in the longer term is interventions to prevent people from being forced to sleep rough in the first place."

She urged departments across government to work together to address the issue - saying too many people being discharged from hospital or leaving care were ending up on the streets.

Sarah Elliott, Shelter's chief executive, called Burnham's pledge a "game-changing move".

She said "tackling the most visible form of homelessness is a strong start" but urged the prime minister to act on his promise to build more council houses to help people living in temporary accommodation.

The shadow housing secretary said Burnham promised to end rough sleeping while Manchester mayor "and failed because he didn't do the hard work necessary".

James Cleverly added that families would fear there would be tax rises unless Labour could "come clean on what other programmes they are cutting to pay for this project".

Liberal Democrat housing spokesperson Gideon Amos said: "Sticking plasters won't fix the homelessness crisis. Without a proper long-term plan, people could simply find themselves back on the streets once the festive headlines fade."

He urged Burnham to commit to a Lib Dem target to build 150,000 social homes every year.

Deputy Reform UK leader Richard Tice also criticised Burnham's efforts to tackle homelessness while Manchester mayor, and described the government's new plans as "yet another vague announcement with no substances which uses our most vulnerable for political point-scoring".

News.title: British couple on honeymoon killed in helicopter crash on Greek island
News.content:
A young British couple and their pilot were killed in a helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, Greek police have said.

They have been named as newlyweds Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert, who were in Greece on their honeymoon.

The private Bell 206 helicopter crashed just metres from a landing pad, killing the pair and their pilot, a Greek national.

The couple are said to have taken the helicopter from the village of Markopoulo near Athens to the popular holiday island, Kathimerini reported.

Greece's aviation safety authority told the BBC it was investigating the crash and that its investigators were heading to the scene on Tuesday to gather evidence and speak to witnesses.

News.title: Burnham received £345,000 of donations ahead of becoming PM
News.content:
Andy Burnham has registered accepting Â£345,000 of donations over the past year including Â£164,347 from businessman Lord Sainsbury.

The donations, listed in the most recent version of the MPs' register of interests,, external are the prime minister's first declarations since he was elected to Parliament in June.

Separately, Burnham has also listed hospitality and gifts he received in the year before he returned to Parliament, including trips to Glastonbury, Lancashire Cricket Club and the Aintree Racecourse.

A Labour Party spokesperson said: "It's right that political campaigns are funded by the generous support of party donors, rather than via the public purse.

"All declarations have been made in line with Parliamentary and Electoral Commission rules."

New MPs are required to register all their current financial interests, and any registrable benefits (other than earnings) received in the 12 months before their election within one month of their election.

Lord Sainsbury's donations went towards Burnham's campaign to become Labour leader. Businessman Gary Lubner and former Greater Manchester night-time economy tsar Sacha Lord donated Â£25,000 and Â£35,000 to the campaign respectively.

The TV production company Charlie Parsons Creative contributed Â£50,000 and the think tank ThinkLabour, formerly known as Labour Together, provided Â£22,186.

The donations included the provision of office space, IT equipment, staffing, polling, travel, social media support and message testing.

Burnham's list also includes Â£20,000 of donations towards mayoral campaigning from the trade unions Unison, the Communications Workers Union and the Fire Brigades Union.

Labour peer Lord Blunkett appears on the list having donated Â£2,000 towards Burnham's campaign to become the MP for Makerfield.

Gifts and hospitality Burnham accepted when he was mayor of Greater Manchester include:

Four tickets to Glastonbury, where he was speaking at an event, from the festival organisers and Â£1,000 for accommodation from the campaigning group PRS for Music

Tickets worth Â£3,800 to the Brit Awards in Manchester from Sony Music Entertainment

Two tickets worth Â£500 for the Aintree Racecourse from the Jockey Club Racecourse

Two tickets, valued at Â£458, from Lancashire Cricket Club for a game in The Hundred tournament

A hamper basket and Wedgewood tea set worth Â£340 from the ambassador of Qatar

Shortly after becoming prime minister in 2024, Sir Keir Starmer became embroiled in a row over the gifts he had accepted including tickets to a Taylor Swift concert and thousands of pounds for clothes.

He subsequently paid back more than Â£6,000 worth of gifts and hospitality. He also tightened the rules so that serving ministers had to consider "the need to maintain the public's confidence in the standard of propriety" when accepting gifts.

News.title: How soon will the drought be over?
News.content:
It is the question many people are asking: when will the drought be over, and how much rain will it take for things to return to normal?

Contrary to public perception, a drought does not end with a few days of rain.

Water must flow back into rivers, reservoirs, and the stores beneath our feet in the tiny spaces between soil, sand, and rock. This can take months.

According to scientists, the key question is not "Has it rained?" but "have water resources recovered?"

News.title: Earl Spencer to 'tell the truth' about his sister Princess Diana in new book
News.content:
Earl Spencer is to publish a new book telling the life story of his sister, Diana, Princess of Wales, from his perspective.

Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is due to be released in the UK next month, nearly 30 years after she died.

"I want to speak on Diana's behalf and do so in an openly positive way," Earl Spencer said of his reasons for writing the book.

He added that he hoped it would enable people to understand who she really was: "A one-off, dynamic character, full of love, charisma and self-doubt, who gave life a hell of a go, and left the world a far better place, despite exiting the stage while still so young."

Princess Diana, who died aged 36 following a car crash in Paris in 1997, would have turned 65 on 1 July this year.

Her sons Prince William and Prince Harry were aged 15 and 12 respectively at the time of her death.

In a statement released on Tuesday to mark the new book, Earl Spencer said he had been "inundated yet again" with requests for interviews about his sister, with the 30th anniversary of her death approaching.

"This has convinced me to write down my own thoughts and memories, once and for all, rather than having the discomfort of again reading the opinions of others, many of which are based on untruths that have become accepted over time," he said.

"The aim of this book is to tell the truth about Diana from her brother's perspective, just as I attempted to do when speaking at her funeral," he added, referring to the eulogy he delivered in Westminster Abbey in September 1997.

He said he hoped the book would be of interest to those who "still cherish" Diana's memory from when she was alive.

"And I would be delighted if those too young to remember her in her heyday feel - after reading this - that they 'get' who she really was," he continued.

News.title: Tracking USS Lincoln's months-long mission as concerns about conditions grow
News.content:
There have been reports of poor conditions on board the USS Abraham Lincoln, which the US Navy says will soon be brought home from the Middle East.

The aircraft carrier was originally expected back in May - but the US war with Iran has kept it at sea for around 250 days straight.

BBC Verify has used satellite imagery to monitor the warship's movements which last docked in December last year.
