News.title: One dead and hundreds ill in UK salmonella outbreak
News.content:
Symptoms include stomach cramps, diarrhoea, vomiting or fever. These usually develop between 12 and 72 hours after becoming infected.

Anyone who is concerned should contact their GP or out of hours service in the first instance, says the UKHSA.

Most cases - 199 of the 207 - have been in England, including 47 in London and 38 in Yorkshire and Humber.

There have been six cases in Scotland, one in Wales and another in Northern Ireland.

Hannah Charles, lead epidemiologist for gastrointestinal infections at UKHSA, said: "We're working with Food Standards Agency and other public health agencies to investigate a salmonella outbreak that may be linked to eggs imported from outside of the UK."

Salmonella can be found in a number of food sources including raw or under-cooked poultry or meat and eggs.

Preparing and cooking food thoroughly can prevent infection, as well as washing your hands after using the bathroom and before handling food.

Thousands of cases of food poisoning happen each year in the UK caused by lots of different strains of salmonella.

It is more unusual to see an outbreak like this linked to one specific strain of the bacterium affecting many people at one time.

Experts say it is likely there could be more cases to come and some people may have been unwell but not reported it.

The UKHSA says "extensive" epidemiological and food chain investigations are ongoing to identify the source but that egg consumption remains the strongest to date.

People appear to have fallen ill after eating out rather than after consuming food prepared at home.

Some of the food businesses linked to 24 of the cases use imported eggs.

"At this time there is no identified link to UK-produced eggs or poultry," says the UKHSA.

Any extra precautions or preventative measures will be implemented if needed, it says. The risk to the general public is low.

Jacquelyn McCormick, Head of Incidents at the Food Standards Agency, said eggs which are thoroughly cooked and handled hygienically should not present a food safety risk.

She advised: "Infants, young children, pregnant people and older adults should only eat runny or raw eggs if they have a British Lion mark or are produced under the Laid in Britain egg assurance scheme."

People handling eggs, eggshells or egg packaging should wash their hands thoroughly with soap and water, she added.

News.title: Join EU migration pact to tackle small boats, says Ed Davey
News.content:
The UK should join the EU's new Migration and Asylum Pact as a way of tackling small boat crossings across the Channel, Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey has said.

The agreement, which came into force in June, aims to speed up the asylum process, increase the number of irregular migrants returned to their home countries and spread responsibility for asylum seekers across the EU.

Sir Ed argues that signing up to the pact would allow the UK to return asylum seekers to the first EU country they entered, thereby "destroying the business model" of the gangs behind the crossings.

Labour said the government's efforts to work with European countries to tackle small boat crossings were "bearing fruit".

A Labour spokesperson said more than 47,000 crossings had been prevented in two years and 70,000 people with no right to be in the UK had been removed.

"There's more to do and that will only happen by working in collaboration with the EU," the spokesperson added.

So far this year, more than 14,000 people have arrived in the UK by small boat - a fall of 43% compared to the previous year.

The EU's new pact, which was nearly 10 years in the making, introduces mandatory screening and an updated database to track those arriving in the bloc.

Under the rules, EU nations must take in migrants from those member states that see the highest number of arrivals - such as Italy and Greece - or instead provide extra funding or resources.

News.title: Prevent not helping children fixated with violence, children's commissioner says
News.content:
The government's counter-extremism programme is not able to deal with the growing number of children being referred to it who are "fixated on violence without a clear ideology", the children's commissioner has said.

Referrals of children to Prevent have risen over the past decade - from 2,918 in 2016-17 to 4,715 in 2024-25 - and Dame Rachel de Souza said most were being sent back to schools without further action.

Dame Rachel said most children being referred did not identify with traditional forms of extremism and "stronger safeguarding" was needed for this group.

The government said it was reviewing the report and developing further options to "manage those fascinated with extreme violence".

Dame Rachel's report comes just over two years after three girls were killed while attending a dance class in Southport in July 2024.

Their attacker Axel Rudakubana was 17 at the time and had himself been referred to Prevent three times between 2019 and 2021 due to his interest in terrorist attacks and school shootings, but his case too had been closed because he did not have a clear ideology.

Prevent was set up 20 years ago to try to identify future potential terrorists and intervene in their lives, often by challenging hateful ideologies such as far right extremism or support for jihadist violence.

The second phase of the Southport Inquiry is examining how to deal with individuals who pose a risk of extreme violence but where ideology is not the primary driver, as well as the role of the internet and social media in influencing and enabling them.

A Prevent referral is one made to the police when there are concerns that a person may be susceptible to radicalisation or could be at risk of becoming involved in or supporting terrorism. Typically, for children, this process starts with potential concerning behaviour spotted by teachers or social workers.

Most child referrals are made by the education sector including schools - 60% in the year from April 2024 to March 2025.

The report by the children's commissioner found that most of these referrals were being sent back to the education sector because Prevent was not able to effectively deal with their cases - because its focus was on the risk of terrorism which generally means violence being carried out for an ideological objective.

Some 71% of child referrals were found to have "no specific extremist ideology identified".

Dame Rachel told the BBC many cases were linked to children being involved in the "most awful online communities, watching other children self-harm and trying to make them do that, obsessed with killers and school shootings" - material she said was illegal under the Online Safety Act.

"Counter-terrorism police and Prevent are excellent at deprogramming children who have been caught into ideological movements," she told BBC Radio 4's World at One programme.

"What they can't deal with is this, so we have to make sure there is a far wider response."

News.title: Fire engulfs London waste centre
News.content:
About 100 firefighters are tackling a massive blaze at a waste facility in south-east London.

Fifteen fire engines were called to Landmann Way in Bermondsey shortly before 20:00 BST after about 50 tonnes of household waste caught fire.

London Fire Brigade (LFB) warned that a large amount of smoke was being produced by the blaze and advised local residents to keep their doors and windows closed.

LFB said the cause of the fire was not yet known, but firefighters tackled a blaze at the same facility in June.

Speaking from the scene, station commander Duncan Rees said: "Crews are working hard in difficult conditions to bring the fire under control."

He added that a 32m ladder and a 64m ladder were being used to tackle the flames from above.

News.title: Two more officers arrested in Police Federation fraud investigation
News.content:
Four more people, including two serving police officers, have been arrested as part of an investigation into suspected fraud and bribery at the Police Federation of England and Wales.

Two men and two women were arrested at the federation's offices in Leatherhead, Surrey, on Tuesday. The women are both in their 50s and the men in their 40s and 50s.

The City of London Police's corruption unit, which leads on fraud investigations, said all four suspects had been taken to a police station for questioning. It comes after three arrests connected to the same case were made in March.

The Police Federation represents more than 145,000 rank-and-file officers, up to and including the rank of chief inspector as well as special constables.

Det Supt Jim Halkett said the investigation "continues to make significant progress, with officers working through a number of lines of inquiry to establish the full facts and circumstances surrounding this case".

Police said the four people arrested on Tuesday were being questioned on suspicion of fraud by abuse of position of trust. One of the women and the man in his 50s were also being held on suspicion of bribery and fraud by failing to disclose.

It comes after the three men were arrested in March on suspicion of fraud by abuse of position - a 51-year-old from Wales, a 55-year-old from Bristol and a 46-year-old from Surrey.

Police said the three either currently or previously "occupied senior roles within [the Police Federation's] governance and operational structure".

Police Federation chief executive Mukund Krishna is understood to be among the three. The federation confirmed he was suspended from his role "due to an ongoing police investigation" in a statement issued days after the arrests.

News.title: Burnham says he's not embarrassed about hoax message exchange
News.content:
Andy Burnham says he is not embarrassed that he exchanged messages with a person posing as US President Donald Trump's chief of staff.

The prime minister added all politicians face "these challenges" but insisted he did "everything right" in how he handled the security breach.

News website Politico first reported, external that Burnham communicated with a person claiming to be Susie Wiles. Burnham said there was a "minimal exchange of information of zero consequence".

Liberal Democrat MP James MacCleary has written to Parliament's Intelligence and Security Committee (ISC) to ask them to consider investigating what he called an "egregious security breach".

It is understood the communication between Burnham and the person posing as Wiles was in the form of messages and there was no conversation between the two.

Asked if he was embarrassed about the incident, Burnham told broadcasters: "No, I am not because there was a minimal exchange, nothing of consequence and quickly I realised that this needed to be reported and I did so.

"So I handled it in the right way. All politicians are receiving these pressures and these challenges, but I did everything right."

Pressed on what action is being taken to find out who was behind the incident and to improve systems, Burnham said the "correct action" had been taken both in the UK and the US, without providing further details.

MacCleary, in his letter to ISC chairman Lord Beamish, said the security of the prime minister's communications "ought to be an absolute priority".

He added: "We need to understand how this breach could occur, or else risk it being repeated."

News.title: Nigeria influencer arrested after seizure of cocaine worth $28m destined for the UK
News.content:
The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said 184.5kg of cocaine was found concealed in brown boxes at a courier facility in Lagos on Monday 3 August.

The agency said it was being exported by an international trafficking network that for years had used Nigeria as a transit hub to move drugs to the UK, other parts of Europe and to Asia.

Micheal was arrested 10 days later at Lagos's Murtala Mohammed International Airport as he attempted to leave the country on a business-class flight to the French capital.

"Upon credible intelligence that he intended to flee the countryâ¦ our operatives moved decisively and apprehended him at the boarding gateâ¦ just as he attempted to escape the reach of the law," the head of the NDLEA, General Buba Marwa, said.

Micheal was carrying more than $12,840 in cash in three currencies - euros, pounds and naira - as well as expensive jewellery "consistent with the proceeds of his illicit trade" when he was arrested, the agency said.

A second detained suspect, Lawal Mujab Kehinde, is alleged to have been a staff member of a logistics company through which the cocaine was transported.

The NDLEA alleged the 33-year-old packaged cocaine for export and was paid in cash. Kehinde has not commented on the allegations or been charged in court.

The agency said other suspected members of the network in the UK have also been arrested by counterpart law enforcement agencies overseas.

The BBC is chasing the UK authorities for comment.

Marwa said the arrests demonstrated what could be achieved when international agencies worked together and vowed to pursue other members of the network.

"We will track you to the departure gates if we must," he said at a news conference in Lagos.

News.title: Actress Phyllida Law, mother of Emma and Sophie Thompson, dies at 94
News.content:
Born in Glasgow in 1932, Law attended the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, initially to become a stage designer but ended up studying acting instead "by happy accident".

She married fellow actor Eric Thompson - best known for The Magic Roundabout - in 1957.

The couple were together until he died of a heart attack aged 53, in 1982.

Throughout a career spanning eight decades, Law would go on to appear in numerous TV shows including Dixon of Dock Green and Rumpole of the Bailey before Midsomer Murders, Foyle's War, Doc Martin and New Tricks.

She was also known for her work on the big screen in films such as Anna Karenina, Saving Grace and Miss Potter.

On stage, Law appeared alongside Alec Guinness in John Mortimer's A Voyage Round My Father in London's West End in 1971, and in Alan Bennett's Habeas Corpus at the Oxford Playhouse in 1973, which then transferred to the capital.

She also played Jacqueline in the original London cast of La Cage Aux Folles at the London Palladium in 1986.

The prolific character actress starred alongside John Hurt in a short film entitled Love at First Sight which was shortlisted for an Oscar in 2012.

Law received an OBE in 2014 for services to drama and for charitable services.

Her daughters have both gone on to enjoy success on screen.

Emma was born in 1959 and has won two Oscars - one for acting in Howard's End and another for writing the screenplay for Sense and Sensibility - and is also known for featuring in Love Actually and the Harry Potter film series.

Sophie was born in 1964 and has appeared in films including Gosford Park and Four Weddings and a Funeral, and been nominated for seven Olivier Awards on stage.

Speaking about her daughters to the Telegraph in 2017, external, Law said: "They are both my colleagues in a way. They didn't follow in our footsteps, they rushed past us, trampling on us."

The family acting dynasty has continued with Dame Emma's daughter Gaia, who posted on Instagram about her grandmother: "Rest well my queen."

Speaking of her love of the arts to the same newspaper, Law joked: "I've got to have my funeral in the afternoon, curtain up 2.30pm, so people can get to the theatre afterwards."

News.title: Wetherspoons bans customers playing music from phones in pubs
News.content:
Wetherspoons has banned its customers from playing music out loud or taking calls on speaker, saying the noise from phones and tablets was an increasing problem driving people "nuts".

The company â which runs 792 pubs and bars across the UK â said that following complaints it has asked customers to switch their devices to silent or to use earphones.

Polling in recent years by various organisations suggests people are largely opposed to others playing music or taking calls on speaker in public spaces.

Wetherspoons told the BBC that staff would be asked to use "common sense" when enforcing the ban.

"We are not looking to ask anyone to leave a pub if they go against the ruling, but it is an option for managers if they refuse to do so," the company said.

The British Beer and Pub Association, which represents Wetherspoons and several other pub companies in the UK, said that "having a clear policy helps staff enforce rules and customers know what they can and can't do".

The group added: "We're yet to hear of anyone who relishes having a pint against the backdrop of a speakerphone call or someone loudly playing a video, so we expect this move will be greatly welcomed."

A fire near railway lines in London has resulted in cancelled services as around 100 firefighters tackle the blaze.

Network Rail a major fire near the railway has closed all lines between London Bridge and New Cross. Significant smoke is affecting the area and it is unsafe for trains to pass.

A statement on the National Rail website said: “A fire on a property between London Bridge / Canada Water and New Cross / New Cross Gate means all lines are blocked.

“As a result, trains between these stations may be cancelled, severely delayed by up to 100 minutes or revised.”

Major disruption is expected until the end of the day.

The fire is at a waste facility on Landmann Way in Deptford, near to train lines which run to London Bridge Station. The cause of the blaze is not yet known.

Smoke and flames from a blaze on Landmann Way, in Deptford as seen from Millwall ( PA )

In a statement, London Fire Brigade said: “Fifteen fire engines and around 100 firefighters are responding to a fire on Landman Way, Deptford.

“The fire involves around 50 tonnes of household waste stored at a waste facility. This will be a protracted incident, with firefighting operations expected to be taking place through the night.”

Speaking from the scene, station commander Duncan Rees said: "Crews are working hard in difficult conditions to bring the fire under control. One of the Brigade’s 32m ladders and a 64m ladder are both being used as a water towers to tackle the flames from above

"A large amount of smoke is being produced by the incident. Local residents should keep doors and windows closed where possible."

The brigade took the first of over 160 calls reporting the incident at 7.59pm, and crews from East Greenwich, Old Kent Road, Deptford and surrounding fire stations have been sent to the scene.

People have been asked to avoid the area and keep their doors and windows closed where possible because of the large amount of smoke.

Maintaining good sleep habits in middle age could help people stay in the workforce for longer, research suggests.

By contrast, regularly disturbed sleep or resting for nine hours or more was associated with leaving employment up to nine months earlier.

To evaluate the impact of rest on career duration, researchers in Finland examined data from individuals aged 50 to 68.

They analysed two separate studies: one involving more than 70,000 public sector workers between 2000 and 2016, and a second monitoring 6,071 Finnish adults from 1998 to 2013.

Data on sleep was collected after people turned 50, and was categorised as either short (under seven hours), mid-range (seven to eight and a half hours) and long (nine or more hours).

Sleeping for lengthy periods of nine hours or more, or being disturbed regularly, were linked to leaving the workforce up to nine months earlier ( Alamy/PA )

Disturbances included problems falling or staying asleep and waking too early.

People who reported no disturbances had a working life expectancy of 13 years five months.

This was compared with 13 years among those moderately disturbed two to four nights a week, and 12 years 10 months among people whose sleep was disturbed almost every night.

The longest working life expectancy – almost 14 years – was among professional women who reported no sleep disturbances.

The shortest – almost 12.5 years – was among men with severe sleep disturbances.

Elsewhere, public sector workers who slept from under seven to eight and a half hours had a working life expectancy of 13 years two months, while those who slept for more than nine hours were expected to work 12 years five months.

Researchers also found a difference in working life expectancy between professional workers with higher levels of education and those in routine jobs with lower levels of education.

Among 50-year-old public sector workers, the longest life expectancy was around 13 years seven months among men and women in professional roles and short sleep lengths.

The shorted was six years five months, among men in routine jobs with low levels of education who slept for more than nine hours a night.

Researchers said the findings, published in the journal Occupational & Environmental Medicine, suggest healthy sleep may help people keep working as they age.

“To promote older adults’ participation in working life, supporting sleep of recommended length and good quality may be required,” they added.

Rodri has completed his move to Barcelona from Manchester City.

The midfielder, named player of the tournament during Spain’s World Cup triumph this summer, completed a £65.4million transfer on Tuesday after undergoing his medical with the club.

He has signed a four-year deal at the Camp Nou.

Rodri spent seven seasons at City, helping them win the Premier League title on four occasions and scoring the decisive goal as they beat Inter Milan in the 2023 Champions League final.

“Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement for Rodri, who is committing to the Catalan club until June 30 2030,” read a statement from the LaLiga champions on their website.

Barca’s statement added Rodri is “considered one of the best players in the world in his position”, adding he “stands out for his tactical intelligence, composure on the ball, ability to regain possession and precision in his passing”.

Rodri flew to Barcelona’s El Prat airport on Monday ahead of the finishing touches to his move being finalised and told reporters: “Playing for Barcelona is a dream come true for me.”

Rodri, who joined from Atletico Madrid in July 2019 when City paid a then club-record £62.6m, had entered into the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium.

Barcelona saw an initial £40m offer and an increased bid turned down before an agreement was struck on Sunday, despite new City boss Enzo Maresca admitting he wanted to keep the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner.

open image in gallery Rodri said ‘playing for Barcelona is a dream come true for me’ ( Reuters )

While an anterior cruciate ligament injury in the 2024-25 season and hamstring and groin problems in the 2025-26 season – Pep Guardiola’s last at the club – have restricted his involvement, he was at his best for Spain in North America.

In a message to City fans on the club’s website, Rodri wrote: “I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life but I am going to try.

“I knew I came into a top team but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect.

“We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it. And the fans were with us every step of the way.

“City didn’t just make me grow as a player. They made me grow as a human. I saw my brother graduating from Manchester Metropolitan University. I could see my girlfriend working for the NHS.

“Manchester shaped my whole life. It’s time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my team-mates. This journey couldn’t be the same without you, my heart will always be blue.”

City have already seen club captain and Rodri’s fellow midfielder Bernardo Silva walk out the door this summer after joining Real Madrid on a free transfer, while they have agreed a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah.

However, Elliot Anderson has joined from Nottingham Forest for £116m and City have also been linked with Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

Children's lives could be saved by creating more clean air zones, the mother of a girl who died after exposure to excessive air pollution has said after a new study linked air quality improvements following the introduction of London’s ultra low emission zone (Ulez) to improved lung growth in young people.

Rosamund Adoo-Kissi-Debrah, whose daughter Ella became the first person in the UK to have air pollution listed as a cause of death,said “London children shouldn’t be the only ones who are breathing clean air” after research suggested the impact of air pollution on lung development in children could be reversed by removing or reducing air pollution.

A team of scientists led by Queen Mary University of London measured and monitored the lung health of more than 3,400 children aged six to nine on annual school visits between 2018 and 2022.

They recruited the children from 84 primary schools in London and Luton, with Luton acting as a comparison site because it has a similar mix of traffic pollutants but no clean air zone.

Experts say those who do not have fully developed lungs by early adulthood face increased risks of respiratory conditions, such as asthma, cardiovascular and metabolic disease and premature death as adults.

open image in gallery London’s ultra low emission zone (ULEZ) was first introduced in 2019 ( PA )

According to the study, initial lung capacity measurements taken before Ulez was introduced showed that children in London had significantly smaller lungs compared with children living in Luton.

However, the data collected over the five years indicated that London children’s lung size and health accelerated and improved to be comparable with that of children in Luton as the zone was implemented.

Over the period, the percentage of children with impaired lung function in London fell from 14 per cent to 9 per cent, compared to 9 and 7 per cent in Luton. The findings demonstrated that these improved lung growth trajectories were strongly related to air quality improvements, the scientists said.

Ms Adoo-Kissi-Debrah has welcomed the research and is calling on the prime minister and mayors across the country to introduce new clean air zones across the UK, as well as a new Clean Air Act.

She lived in Lewisham, just outside the South Circular, with her daughter Ella who died from an asthma attack in 2013 at just eight years old.

open image in gallery Rosamund Adoo-Kissi-Debrah ( PA )

Five years after Ella’s death, in April 2019, London mayor Sadiq Khan introduced the Ulez zone for the capital - which involves a charge for drivers each day they enter any London borough in a more polluting vehicle.

Ms Adoo-Kissi-Debrah said that after Ella’s inquest, the mayor of London was urged to extend London’s clean air zone and tackle the “public health emergency” posed by air pollution.

In 2022, Sir Chris Whitty, the government’s chief medical officer, published his annual report urging faster action to improve air quality across the country and tackle sources of air pollution.

She told The Independent: “The reason Ella passed away was due to the fumes she was breathing on the South Circular. For me, as her mother, 13 years on, I know she didn’t die in vain. Ella’s legacy has spurred this on.

“My message to all the mayors is we need to find a way... London children shouldn’t be the only ones who are breathing clean air. It should be all over the UK...what this study is about is reducing emissions; we have to reduce our exposure.

“For a lot of children, the hope I have is their lungs can be restored.”

One of the lead authors, Chris Griffiths, professor of Primary Care at Queen Mary University of London, said: “Lung function is a strong predictor of health in later life, predicting increased mortality and increased risk of chronic diseases, stroke, diabetes, cancer, respiratory diseases as well. So lower lung function, entering adulthood, is associated with increased risk of disease and adverse outcomes.”

He added: “Traffic pollution in cities damages children’s health and development... We provide the strongest evidence yet on how these harms can be prevented. Ambitious clean air zones should be considered a priority for cities globally with traffic-related air pollution.”

Professor Griffiths said the study was also consistent with reviews on the impacts of cleaner air zones globally and was consistent with the benefits seen in Bradford, where a form of clean air zone was introduced in 2022, and has been linked to a reduction in GP appointments in the city.

He added that in London there had been evidence showing a relationship between ULEZ and hospital admissions.

Dr Ian Mudway, senior lecturer in the School of Public Health at Imperial College London, said that air pollution was associated with poorer lung growth in children overall, regardless of where they live.

Mayor of London Sir Sadiq Khan, who oversaw Ulez’s introduction, said: “Introducing and expanding ULEZ involved incredibly difficult decisions.“It was very tough, and a vocal minority backed by vested interests made it extremely difficult, but I refused to stand by while air pollution continued to damage Londoners’ health.

“This research proves we were right to act and reinforces my decision to extend the benefits of cleaner air to every child in London.”

The study, which involved researchers from Imperial College London, the universities of Bedfordshire, Oxford, Cambridge, Edinburgh and Southern California, with funding from the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR), was published in The Lancet journal.

Netflix is looking to cast people who have undergone a major body transformation for its new reality dating series, Weight to Date.

The streamer announced Tuesday that the unscripted dating show will follow singles “during and after extreme weight loss as they navigate dating, identity, and the search for lasting love.”

Included in the press release is a link to the website www.WeightToDateCasting.com to apply for the debut season. At the top of the form is the question, “Are you ready to find love after a significant body change?”

It adds: “This new inspiring dating series will highlight the journeys of selected singles who are discovering what dating is like after a major body transformation.”

Applicants must be at least 18 years old and a legal U.S. resident.

open image in gallery New Netflix dating series, 'Weight to Date,' will feature singles who have undergone a major body transformation ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Streamer put out an open casting call for people to apply to be on the debut season ( AFP/Getty )

According to Deadline, the series will follow more of a documentary format, focusing on 10 to 12 people, some of whom have lost a drastic amount of weight and are ready to enter the dating scene.

Weight to Date is just Netflix’s latest unscripted dating series, following Age of Attraction, which mixed 40 singles between the ages of 22 and 60. Its portfolio also includes Love is Blind, where singles date through a wall and get engaged sight-unseen, Temptation Island and the seven-time Emmy-winning reality show Love on the Spectrum.

A premiere date for Weight to Date has not yet been announced.

The show arrives at a time when weight-loss drugs, specifically GLP-1 injectables Ozempic and Wegovy, are surging in popularity in the U.S.

Data collected by Gallup found that GLP-1 usage has nearly quadrupled since 2024, up from 3 percent to 11 percent in 2026.

open image in gallery GLP-1 drug usage in the U.S. has surged in recent years ( PA )

Ozempic was first approved by the FDA in 2017 as a treatment for type 2 diabetes. In 2021, it became a top choice among celebrities and influencers to curb appetites and therefore shed weight.

That same year, the maker of Ozempic launched Wegovy, an FDA-approved solution to help with chronic weight management.

Several famous faces, including tennis superstar Serena Williams and This Is Us actor Chrissy Metz, have opened up about their use of GLP-1 drugs. Both Williams and Metz have even signed on with Ro, a telehealth company, as ambassadors to promote its weight-loss medications and platform.

“I’m not getting any younger,” Metz told People in August of her decision to start taking a GLP-1. “I’m in perimenopause, and there were obesity issues within my family and with my father, and I felt like I’ve tried so many modalities, whether it was diets or therapy, and none of it really worked for me.”

A young boy who fell to his death from a 15th-floor window had lived in a "clearly loving environment", an inquest has been told.

Aalim Ahmed died after falling from the kitchen window of a residential tower in Plaistow, east London.

The five-year-old died instantly, with his "distraught" father Makail Ahmed running down from the top-floor temporary social housing flat to find his son's body shortly before 6am on 16 May 2024.

Mr Ahmed and the child's mother, Sahra Osman, have blamed Newham Council and described his death as "preventable", following reports that Ms Osman had repeatedly raised safety concerns about the property.

Aalim’s parents stepped out of the proceedings at Walthamstow Coroners’ Court when audio capturing his final moments was played.

The couple left the room on Tuesday while grainy CCTV audio recorded outside the building was played to those present.

A young child’s voice is twice heard counting down “3, 2, 1” and “a loud clang” follows some seconds later, according to a statement read on behalf of Detective Constance Joe Linton who carried out a review of CCTV footage outside Jacobs House.

He added that after the commotion, “you can hear another young child shouting ‘Aalim'”, who would appear to be the boy’s brother who was then three years old.

Mr Ahmed was “topless and clearly distressed in the footage” as he found his son, DC Linton told the court.

DC Linton said “it is most likely from the footage available” that Aalim had “jumped out” of the flat at Jacobs House in New City Road “of his own accord without the presence of a third party”.

A post-mortem examination found Aalim died from “multiply injuries due to or as a consequence of trauma” from a “fall from height.”

Detective Inspector Jamie Humm, who investigated the incident, said there was “no evidence or suspicion he (Aalim) had been forced.”

“The flat was well furnished and it was clearly a loving environment for a child,” he noted.

He added the soon after arriving at the scene he was satisfied “there was no evidence of a crime not that I thought there would be,.”

Ms Osman has told the court she was “scared” and “horrified” when Newham Council put them in the top-floor flat, which needed repairs, stating that Aalim was autistic, had “no sense of danger” and the place was not suitable for her young family, which also included a newborn baby girl.

open image in gallery Aalim Ahmed’s parents described their son’s death as “preventable” and blamed Newham Council, after claims Ms Osman reported safety concerns about the flat on multiple occasions ( Google Maps )

Despite engineers having been to look at the repairs, she felt the flat was still not safe and there were “open windows”, according to Ms Osman.

All the windows were closed before the family went to bed, the inquest heard.

Aalim could have been climbing to get a biscuit from a cupboard but the windows had “faulty” restrictors and her ongoing complaints to get them fixed led only to a series of workmen who did not sort the problem, she said.

Biscuits were found on the kitchen table but it is still not known how the child would have got to the window, the court heard.

Assistant coroner Ian Wade, who described the audio recording as “poignant”, said: “Aalim at his tender age and with his autism could not have known what could have happened.

“It seems to me that he would not have meant to have deliberately taken the stance to have harmed himself.”

Robert O’Sullivan, of the London Ambulance Service, recalled that “a number of colleagues were visibly shocked” after finding the boy and as a cordon was placed around the building.

In his statement, he recalled: “There was an adult male shouting ‘I have told them about the window’.”

He was not sure if this meant it had been reported to the council.

The right-hand kitchen window was open and the room was cordoned off.

Sergeant Christopher Diment, who was among the officers who attended the scene, said Mr Ahmed was “clearly distraught, pacing around and shouting”, and was “overcome with grief”.

When they went into the flat Mr Ahmed was saying something about the state of the windows, he told the court.

Ms Osman has denied any suggestion she may have “forced” the window open to cope in hot weather.

Successful smoke and fire alarm tests were carried out in April 2024 and the council engineer also noted there was mould in the bedroom and kitchen, an extractor needed repair and a living room window latch needing fixing.

Ms Osman told the inquest she used this opportunity to tell him that the kitchen window also needed to be fixed, but the engineer says the living room latch was the only a problem mentioned.

Aalim’s family had worked with an occupational therapist to help support his needs.

His teacher Esme Johns said the boy had to be reminded not to do or touch something because he “lacked danger awareness”.

She added “he would say sorry, but found it difficult to understand”.

The hearing continues.

A former Venezuelan baseball player currently working for the San Diego Padres was detained by federal immigration officers after arriving in Texas on a work trip for the club, according to statements from his family on Tuesday.

Oswaldo Pirela, who serves as a catching coordinator in the Padres' minor league pipeline, was being held at an El Paso detention center, federal records indicate. In an issued statement, the Padres acknowledged the arrest and noted the club is actively working to gather further details.

His sister, Daniela Pirela, said the father of two was arrested around 5 a.m. Sunday at an El Paso airport. The Padres operate a minor league affiliate team in the Texas border city, known as the El Paso Chihuahuas.

open image in gallery Oswaldo Pirela was being held at an El Paso detention center, federal records show ( AP Photo/Brandon Sloter )

Daniela said her 34-year-old brother has lived in the U.S. for 12 years and has followed the law. She said he applied for asylum in 2015 and lives in Peoria, Arizona, with his wife and two children, ages 9 and 4, who are both U.S. citizens.

“Since he arrived in this country, the only thing he’s done is follow the rules of this country and do things properly,” Daniela told The Associated Press.

The Department of Homeland Security said Oswaldo entered the country legally in 2014 and was granted permission to stay until February 10, 2018. He then “overstayed his welcome,” DHS said in a statement, adding that work authorization or pending applications “do not confer” U.S. legal status.

Owswaldo is in ICE custody pending removal, DHS said.

His family told NBC News that he came to the U.S. from Venezuela and sought asylum but was unaware of why his case had taken so long to process.

Oswaldo’s brother, Jorge Heli Pirela, wrote in an Instagram post, "My brother is not a criminal. He is a son, a brother, a coach, a worker, and a man who came to this country seeking protection after our family suffered persecution in Venezuela. He followed the asylum process, built a life here, worked hard, contributed to his community, and was traveling for work when ICE detained him. We are asking for one thing: due process and justice."

Oswaldo had a brief minor-league playing career as a catcher in the Texas Rangers organization.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

Telegraph Fantasy Football managers need to make compromises to fit in fantasy heavyweights like Erling Haaland (£8.3m) and Bruno Fernandes (6.5m). Brian Brobbey (£3.3m)

The Sunderland forward had a steady Premier League debut season, netting seven times and helping the Black Cats qualify for the Europa League. Harry Wilson (£3.2m)

The midfielder swapped London for Yorkshire in the summer, as he looks to expand on a whopping 17 attacking returns from last season. Feeding the rejuvenated Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£3.9m), and adding goals from midfield for Leeds will be two primary objectives for the Welsh international, who could make a mockery of his mere marginal price increase.



James Trafford (£3.0m)

Another Leeds United summer acquisition, Daniel Farke fought off rival Premier League suitors to land the ex-Manchester City shot-stopper. Leeds United have a mixed bag in terms of opening fixture difficulty, but do have three home league games in the first five before the international break, and the new no.1 has an outside chance of getting the nod in the Carabao Cup games too, so there are points available should the Whites be able to shut out the opposition.



James Hill (£2.6m)

As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub, will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

Five best fantasy football players





Take a look at these elite Telegraph Fantasy Football tips below:



Erling Haaland (£8.3m)

Comfortably last season’s top points scorer with 254, the Norwegian striker will once again likely be the first name in TFF Managers’ XIs. Having come back late from his post-World Cup break, there may be nervousness about early-season minutes. However, if he keeps up his phenomenal August goals-to-games ratio, starting without him may mean playing catch-up against the field.



João Pedro (£5.1m)

Having missed out on the Brazilian squad for the World Cup, the forward looks rejuvenated after a rested summer, netting seven times and assisting twice more in pre-season. With no European distractions for the Blues this season, and attacking intent shown in new manager Xabi Alonso’s selections thus far, the 24-year-old looks primed for a successful season.



Antoine Semenyo (£4.9m)

Perhaps one of the biggest surprises in the pricing for the new season was the City winger’s sub-£5m tag. The January recruit was the second-highest scorer in the game last season, and has looked the most dangerous of Enzo Moresca’s attacking assets in pre-season, so looks the stand-out midfield option.



Gabriel Magalhães (£4.9m)

Another that perhaps warranted a higher price increase, the Brazilian only missed out on breaking the 200-point barrier due to his injury late in the season. While there are cheaper options in the champions’ backline, including Christhian Mosquera (£3.7m), who looks likely to deputise for the injured William Saliba (£4.6m), getting the assurances over long-term starts and the additional attacking returns is enough to warrant paying the higher expense.

The England international has incurred a position change in TFF, and will now gain points for clean sheets as a defender on top of his attacking returns. Had he scored as a defender last season, he would have topped his position table; therefore, £4.2m seems too good value to turn down.

News.title: Rabies deaths are rising. What is going wrong?
News.content:
In a packed intensive care ward in Dhaka, three-year-old Abdul lay paralysed, his tiny body contorted by a rabies infection that had reached his brain.

His mother, Sheuli Akter, 38, sat at his side massaging his legs in the hope that this might loosen his muscles, but it was having no effect. Even his hands and feet were seized up by cramps.

Abdul had been in the hospital for a month but doctors said he was unlikely to live much longer. The infection, they said, had progressed to degenerative encephalitis; the virus had got to his brain.

Abdul was shaking, gripped by fever. His breathing was rapid and panicked, punctuated occasionally by groans of pain.

On his chin was the telltale scar of a dog bite, the source of the infection.

“He was playing outside with the other children,” said Sheuli. “The dog, which was one of those always waiting around outside, suddenly attacked him. They said it went for him because he was the smallest.”

News.title: Arsenal hunger is ominous for rivals as they dismantle Man City
News.content:
Was it the early goal that should have put Arsenal’s rivals on red alert? No. While Ricardo Calafiori’s intervention was dramatic, it wasn’t that. Was it the seamless introduction of the new signings, then? No, it wasn’t that either, despite the excellence of Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis.

How about the emphatic scoreline – surely that was it? Again, the answer is no. Three unanswered goals against Manchester City will always grab a headline, but scorelines do not always define the nature of a performance or a team’s capabilities.

So what was it that should have those with pretensions of ripping Arsenal’s crown from their grasp shuffling uncomfortably? One word: hunger. The reason this was such an ominous afternoon for the chasing pack is the fact Mikel Arteta’s team played with intensity of a team with everything to prove.

Title wins can sometimes sate ambition. Players don’t always want to climb the same mountain again, not least if reaching the peak was initially so draining, but everywhere you looked on a day when Cardiff was painted red and white was evidence that Arsenal remain ravenous for success.

First Guimarães pounced out of the shadows to mug Jérémy Doku, leaving him in a heap. Then there was Gabriel Magalhães thundering into a befuddled Doku, celebrating in front of City’s fans as if he had scored, before Ben White flung himself in front of the Belgian, denying a clear-cut scoring opportunity.

News.title: Rashford returns and Fernandes misses another penalty as Man Utd humbled by Amorim
News.content:
At his AC Milan unveiling, Amorim was asked about the learnings from his United tenure that he would take into his new role. He said: “The first thing is it’s hard to explain the mistakes because for that I would have to explain the context of the last adventure.

“It’s hard to say to you every mistake. The only thing I can say is that I learned a lot and I made some mistakes.

“I didn’t have the opportunity, and I’m sorry for that, I didn’t have the opportunity to say something to the Manchester United fans at the moment and I’m really proud to be their coach for a year in that time.

“But now it’s a different history. There are a lot of things that I could do better in the last experience but sometimes it’s like that, you need to learn to find the right spot to reach a different level and that’s my thinking here.

“Everyone learns from their experience. I learned a lot, I did some mistakes I will try to change, there are some thing you will never change but I think I will be a better manager, that’s all.”

Sports.title: Arteta: We want to be the best club in the world
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta is excited to keep building Arsenal after their Premier League win, vowing to make them "the best club in the world".

The Gunners lifted the trophy last season for the first time in 22 years, and have already made moves to bolster their defence of it, with key arrivals such as Christian Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes.

Arteta says they will keep targeting elite players to get Arsenal to the very top.

"It's certainly the ambition of the club and the owners to be the best club in the world," he told Sky Sports at a Premier League launch event ahead of their Friday night opener against Coventry, live on Sky.

"In order to do that, you need the best facilities, the best stadium, the best supporters, and you need the best squad and the best players in the world.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Savundra and Michael Bridge discuss were Arsenal need to strengthen this summer.

"Those are the ones that win you football matches and the ones that can be decisive when it matters.

"That's what we try to build with the actual players that we have, and with the players that we want to sign to make the difference for Arsenal."

Arsenal go into the season as outright favourites to retain their title, with that status further underlined by their comfortable 3-0 win over Manchester City in Sunday's Community Shield.

Arteta, however, says he is more than comfortable with the position of being the frontrunners.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains why Arsenal's emphatic win over Manchester City has led to plenty of transfer debates for the Gunners.

"I think this is part of our industry, and that's OK," he said. "For me, it's when I look into the eyes of my players and I see that fire, that desire and the will to be better every single day.

"That's the only thing that I care about."

The weight of history is against Arsenal defending their trophy, however. Arsenal have not defended the top-flight title since the 1990s.

It is another milestone Arteta is keen to overcome.

"That's an opportunity that we have ahead, and we are very conscious of what it's going to take to deliver that," he said.

"But I feel the ambition, I feel the desire, and I feel the ability and the conviction around the team that we can do it."

Arsenal chief: New signings need 'to change the dial'

Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick says the club want to sign players who "are going to change the dial".

The Premier League champions missed out on Vinicius Junior after he signed a new Real Madrid contract, while they are interested in Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez.

Asked about the club being linked with elite players, Garlick said: "It's players that are going to take Arsenal forward.

Image: Arsenal's Bruno Guimaraes during the friendly against Como

"In the past we've looked at players that maybe helped build out the squad or get us to a certain level, but now we're competing right at the top level, and we do need to bring in players that are going to change the dial.

"That might be younger players that come into your squad and give them time to develop, and you've seen that in the last couple of years at Arsenal, and if we're able to combine those players that are coming through the academy with some of the best players in the world then we've got every chance of maintaining that success and going beyond what we've already achieved."

Arsenal have spent £143.5m on four summer signings, including the permanent arrival of defender Piero Hincapie.

Questioned on whether there is still money to be spent, Garlick replied: "We said at the start of this season we're about to embark on that we're not going to stand still and pat ourselves on the back and say, 'Well done, job done, nothing else to do'. We want to move forward - the best clubs are always moving forward.

"You can see we've already invested in the squad this season, and if the right opportunity arises, then we will look to strengthen in all areas.

"The window's open for the next couple of weeks, and if there are players that are going to come in and move Arsenal forward, then we will look at that.

"The standard now is high, though - the bar's been set winning the Premier League title and getting to the Champions League final. We're probably fishing in a smaller pool of quality players, and that means that it's tricky to land those players that are going to drive Arsenal forward.

"But if the right opportunity presents itself, we'll certainly be exploring it."

Analysis: Where could Arsenal strengthen before window shuts?

Arsenal showed why they are considered favourites to retain the Premier League with their dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City, but there is still a possibility that Arteta further reinforces his title-winning squad.

They want to add a forward and a defender. Finding a defender who can soften the blow of William Saliba's extended spell out has led Arsenal to hold talks over potential deals for England internationals Ezri Konsa and Jarell Quansah.

Both players share a similar profile and have the capacity to play at centre-back and right-back, but both look to be difficult deals to do. Aston Villa want £60m for Konsa and there is a big gap in valuation, while Bayer Leverkusen do not currently want to sell Quansah.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jamie O'Hara makes his predictions for the new Premier League season, including who he thinks will come out on top as leading goalscorer!

It remains to be seen if Arsenal can achieve their goal of bringing in a statement forward signing after Vinicius Junior chose to stay at Real Madrid. They are interested in Julian Alvarez at Atletico Madrid, while there are also links with Victor Osimhen.

Arsenal had set out to sign a left-winger at the start of the window but will be alert to any opportunities for long-term targets in the final days of the window that could improve the attack in other positions.

Summer signing Christos Tzolis' performance levels have taken many by surprise ahead of the new season, including Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta, which may well convince Arsenal that they have adequately addressed the left-wing position.

Arsenal want to make more from sales this summer in a bid to be more financially sustainable, and they are understood to be willing to listen to offers for Gabriel Martinelli, Ethan Nwaneri and Gabriel Jesus while there is uncertainty around Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Bruno Guimaraes' arrival has raised the prospect of either Lewis-Skelly or Martin Zubimendi departing. However, any deal for Zubimendi would likely require Arsenal to make a return on the £51m they signed him for last summer, while Lewis-Skelly goes down as pure profit.

Sports.title: Venus Williams given US Open wild card - with another held potentially for Serena
Sports.content:
Venus Williams has been given a wild card into the US Open singles draw, and the tournament is keeping one on hold - perhaps in case her sister Serena wants to join her.

Sloane Stephens, the 2017 US Open champion, was one of six other women to receive a wild card, and the US Tennis Association said the final one is still to be announced.

That almost certainly would go to Serena Williams, if she decides she wants to return to the tournament at 44. Coverage of the US Open begins on Sunday August 30, live on Sky Sports Tennis.

Venus received a wild card last year, returning to the tournament she won twice for the first time since 2023.

The 46-year-old became the oldest entrant in singles at the tournament since Renee Richards played at 47 in 1981, according to the International Tennis Federation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Serena and Venus Williams against Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns from the Cincinnati Open

She has continued to play some singles matches and this week joined Serena for their first doubles tournament together since the 2022 US Open. They lost Monday at the Cincinnati Open in a tiebreaker against Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

The sisters planned to play at Wimbledon but had to withdraw after Serena injured her knee in her singles match. That marked her first time playing singles since the 2022 US Open, and she indicated afterwards that she hoped to keep competing if healthy.

Image: The last remaining wild card place is understood to have been held back should Serena Williams decide she wants to compete in singles

Headlining the wild card recipients on the men's side were 39-year-old Gael Monfils, set to play his final Grand Slam tournament before retiring, and Australian Alexei Popyrin, who upset Novak Djokovic in 2024 on the way to the fourth round. One spot is also being held among the eight men's wild cards.

The main draw begins on Sunday August 30, with the qualifying tournaments being played earlier that week.

Watch the ATP and WTA Tours live on Sky Sports. The US Open is also live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with NOW.

Sports.title: Root won't 'rip up' Bazball blueprint as Babar is ruled out for Pakistan
Sports.content:
Returning England Test skipper Joe Root says he feels "as ready as any other England captain", adding he has no plans on "ripping up" the Bazball blueprint that preceded his second stint in charge.

Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, his first permanent spell from 2017 to 2022 ending with a run of just one win in 17 Tests before Ben Stokes took over in step with head coach Brendon McCullum.

But, after an impressive first couple of years to the Bazball era, the 2-1 series defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer saw Stokes retire from international cricket during the final Test and subsequently prompted McCullum's removal as red-ball head coach.

"I don't think there's a huge amount we need to change. It's small things that will make a big difference," Root said ahead of the three-Test series against Pakistan, which starts on Wednesday at Headingley - live on Sky Sports Cricket, from 10am (first ball 11am).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root gives his first interview since being reappointed England Test captain

"It's not about ripping it up, I think it's about keeping a lot of the good stuff we've been doing for a period of time, stuff that Ben and Baz built for a long while.

"I don't believe there is one way of playing Test cricket. You've got to be adaptable and play the situation. It's never the same throughout five days, there's different challenges and you've got to adjust to the ebbs and flows throughout."

As for his own readiness to return to the captaincy, the 35-year-old made it clear he was fully prepared to embrace the challenge one more time.

"The landscape is different," he said. "I'm a different player and person than I was when I [first] took over as captain.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports Cricket podcast, Nasser Hussain fears Joe Root sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes

"I'm in a very fortunate, unique position where I've got 60-odd games of experience to look back on. There are things I might want to change and do slightly differently.

"I had time to step away, play in a different environment, under a different coach, different captain, and see the game from a different lens.

"In many ways I feel as ready as any other England captain that's been before; to have that amount of experience is invaluable."

He added: "I'm really excited. And to get the chance to start at Headingley as well is always nice, my home ground.

"It's a very talented group of players that are very capable of special things. I'm really excited about where we can take this team."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew previously imposed on his team

'Hugely supportive' Brook to remain vice-captain

White-ball skipper Harry Brook, despite serving as Test vice-captain, was overlooked in favour of Root to lead England in Stokes' absence for the second Test against New Zealand at The Oval, as well as for the permanent job upon his international retirement.

Root confirmed Brook will continue in the role as No 2 in the Test team and insisted the pair's bond remains strong.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast Nasser Hussain, believes Harry Brook is a 'very good captain' but needs the 'mature Harry to come out' after his England Test captaincy snub

"Our relationship is exactly as it has been for a long time," he said. "Me and Harry are very good friends and get along well away from cricket, and clearly get the best out of each other when playing together.

"He's been hugely supportive. I fully feel like he's got my back, as the rest of the guys do. He's going to be invaluable.

"He's done some brilliant things already within the white-ball space. He's a brilliant leader within the group and the fact he's not captain, that shouldn't be taken away from him."

As for life without Stokes, Root added: "It's a big void to fill. He's someone who has been ever present for the best part of 15 years.

"It's been different, but we've only been together as a full team for a day and a half."

And quizzed on whether he could yet return to the side, with a home Ashes series on the horizon in 2027, Root said: "Who knows? That's a question for Ben.

"We need to look after the here and now, and that's this series."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England managing director Rob Key does not rule out a return to Test cricket for Ben Stokes and why they chose to appoint Joe Root as captain and not Harry Brook

Pakistan captain Babar injured for Headingley

Pakistan captain Babar Azam has been ruled out of the series opener against England due to a finger injury, with Salman Ali Agha taking temporary charge at Headingley.

Image: Pakistan captain Babar Azam will miss the first Test at Headingley due to an injured finger

Babar was initially struck on the right hand when facing the West Indies earlier this month, before he then received another blow from England Under-19 seamer Manny Lumsden in a tour match at Beckenham last week. He retired hurt in what was described at the time as a "precautionary measure".

The tourists were keen to give him time to recover but, while he has been cleared of a broken middle finger, he has not been cleared to lead his side at Headingley despite working through a brief net session.

"Babar Azam is not available, Salman will be captain," head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said on Tuesday.

"It's not broken, there is a little bit of swelling on the finger. Hopefully he will be available for the second Test match."

Babar's absence robs Pakistan not only of their leader but one of their most talented batters, with nine Test hundreds to his name and a Test average of 43.68. Saud Shakeel is expected to be drafted into the XI after sitting out the West Indies series.

'Relaxed Root looks up for the challenge'

Sky Sports News reporter James Cole:

"It's old shoes for Joe Root; he's got all the experience behind him and he seemed relaxed.

"He is, it's fair to say, inheriting a big rebuilding job. England have lost seven of their last 10 Tests, they've lost their head coach Brendon McCullum and their captain Ben Stokes, who had been such a mainstay of the Test team for so long and led such a unique, attacking brand of cricket called Bazball.

Image: Jordan Cox comes into England's side for just his second Test

"As well as losing Stokes from the middle order, who was the glue and provided balance between the batting and bowling, they've got an opener Emilio Gay who has played just three Test and who is out of nick at the moment, and a rookie at number three in Jordan Cox, who has only batted there once before.

"In place of the talismanic Stokes, Dan Lawrence comes back in and offers a spinning all-rounder option, but he hasn't played a Test in two years.

"It's fair to say Root has got a lot on his hands, but he's up for the challenge."

Watch day one of the first Test between England and Pakistan, at Headingley, live on Sky Sports Cricket and Sky Sports Main Event from 10.15am on Wednesday (11am first ball). Stream cricket and more sport contract-free with NOW.

Sports.title: Rodri completes Barcelona move as Man City pursue replacement
Sports.content:
Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Rodri from Manchester City in a deal worth £65.4m.

The Spain World Cup winner and former Ballon d'Or winner, who helped City win four Premier League titles and a Champions League crown, has signed a four-year contract with the LaLiga club.

Rodri, 30, had one year left on his City contract and, while they wanted him to stay and sign an extension, Barcelona's third offer proved to be too good to turn down.

Barcelona had bids of £40m and £55m rejected by City before the deal was eventually agreed.

Enzo Maresca's side are pursuing replacements for both Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders, who is set to join Saudi Arabian side Al Qadsiah for around £51m.
