IN FULL: Rodri pens City farewell to fans

Rodri has penned a farewell letter to Man City fans after his departure to Barcelona was confirmed.

"Dear City fans, I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life but I am going to try," it said, on the club's official website.

"It's hard to find the words to express how much gratitude, love and support me and my family have experienced all these years.

"I remember how I felt when I arrived, signing for the big Manchester City. It was a moment of pure excitement - 'wow I am going to play with Kevin, Aguero, Silva, Bernardo, John and many others.' I couldn't stop smiling.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Rodri gives an emotional farewell to Manchester City fans after his move to Barca

"And then Pep, waiting to teach me everything from day one. Pep I can tell you now, I couldn't handle all those tactics in my head.

"But a question came to me, 'could we handle all these expectations for the next years.' I think that time answered the question.

"I knew I came into a top team but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect. We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it. And the fans were with us every step of the way.

"Many incredible moments come to my mind.

"My first trophy at City, in my first game.

"The last minute winners, like Arsenal away.

"Scoring in the Villa game to reach the Premier League, when it looked so tough.

"Scoring the goal to win the Champions League that we all wanted so much.

"The incredible reception you gave me after the Balon d'Or. You cannot imagine how proud I am to be the first player to win this award in a sky blue shirt.

"Making history, with the Treble, with Four in a Row. We saw things they'll never see.

"And in the bad moments, also, you never let me down. My first day back on the pitch I realised how much you love me and I understood how special these fans were.

"City didn't just make me a grow as a player. They made me grow as a human.

"I saw my brother graduating from Manchester Metropolitan University.

"I could see my girlfriend working for the NHS.

"Manchester shaped my whole life.

"I will never forget stepping onto the pitch, seeing a sea of blue sing 'nah, nah, nah, nah…CITY', taking my scooter into town for a coffee, walking through the parks listening to Oasis and always loving Manchester's great rain.

"So City fans, it's time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my teammates. This journey couldn't be the same without you, my heart will always be Blue."

Sports.title: Maguire: I want to be greedy about winning trophies
Sports.content:
Sitting down with Harry Maguire for one of his first interviews of the season, I found a player who was reflective but also excited about the future and what's to come.

Maguire is going into his eighth season at Manchester United and has experienced almost every emotion during his time at the club, like the short highs under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the polarising Erik ten Hag period or the ultimately tumultuous time of Ruben Amorim.

However, despite the collective or individual woes over the years, Maguire remains and revels every time in his importance to this squad - which perhaps makes the journey even sweeter.

"To play for this club for one would have been a dream come true when I was a young kid, so to be here going into my eighth season, it's something I'm really proud of," Maguire said.

"It's not about me, but at this stage of my career, I want to be part of a successful team and a team that wins. That's got to be the aim for all the boys this season - we want to be competitive right until the end of the season in every competition."

So with days to go ahead of the 2026/27 season, that is the question - can this Manchester United team compete for the title amongst a league full of change?

Maguire reflected: "We want to improve on last season. Everyone wants to win the Premier League, of course that is going to be our aim, that's what this club demands. We have the belief we can be really competitive and we can beat anyone on our day. It's going to be an exciting season."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Maguire says it's amazing to get another year at Manchester United after signing a new one-year contract at Old Trafford earlier this year

'No doubt this team is different under Carrick'

Having spent a few days around the team in Dublin last week, it is clear there is a comradery and closeness.

It would perhaps be a valid argument that the resetting of the Man Utd changing room culture goes back to Amorim, but nevertheless the squad are benefitting from that having had a successful first six-month spell under Michael Carrick.

For Maguire, he has seen different iterations of Manchester United over the years and he agreed to the notion this squad in particular shares a tight bond.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After signing a new contract for Manchester United, we look at every Premier League goal Harry Maguire has scored for the Red Devils

"During my time at the club, we've had some close groups - no doubt this is one of the closest," Maguire said. "Spending time together and winning football matches brings teams closer.

"Losing that Europa League final, finishing 15th to finishing third and putting the club back in the Champions League, it was a good season but we can't stop here."

There is a certain determination and steel in which Maguire speaks. It could be down to maximising the final years of his career or it could be because he feels the club are close to achieving more silverware.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player At The Open 2026, Manchester United defender Harry Maguire reveals who is the best golfer at the club and sinks an impressive putt

However, it seems unlikely Man Utd can do that without further reinforcements in the transfer window. It is clear they are short at left-back and arguably in midfield with Mason Mount and Manuel Ugarte both injured.

Maguire said: "I'm at an age now where they can bring in as many players as they want, bring in all the best players… I want to win all the trophies and be greedy about it, but it's up to the club.

"I'm sure they're working hard out there to try and bring in the right players, the more the merrier. The stronger the squad, the more opportunity we have of winning these trophies and that's what it's all about when you play for this club."

I'm at an age now where they can bring in as many players as they want, bring in all the best players… I want to win all the trophies and be greedy about it, but it's up to the club.

The future with Heaven and Yoro at the heart of it

Maguire's role in the team has undoubtedly changed. When he joined the club in 2019 for £80m from Leicester City, he was the second most expensive signing in English top-flight history.

Although he is still a key part of Carrick's defence at 33, his role now also involves nurturing the defenders in waiting to one day take his spot.

Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro have both shown huge potential over the last 18 months or so and their time will undoubtedly come, as well as 18-year-old Dan Armer, who has been dubbed by fans on social media as a 'mini Maguire' - a reference Maguire smiles at when I mention him.

Image: Leny Yoro is coming through as one of Man Utd's best young defenders

He enjoys playing a part in mentoring them along the way, adding: "I think that comes quite naturally to me, I want them to have amazing careers.

"Hopefully in five or six years' time, Leny, Ayden and Dan are fighting it out and playing together in this team - that's all I want. They have the attributes and qualities to do that.

"They're young, but they're learning the game under the biggest scrutiny and analysis anyone can imagine and they're only going to get stronger.

"Hopefully one day they're the main two centre-half partnership at this club and they're winning the biggest trophies. Hopefully they're the strongest partnership in world football - that's what they've got to aim to do."

Sports.title: Israel withdraws support for embattled Fifa president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s decision to sack his chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, after the Frenchman’s criticism of the World Cup sell-off plan has hardened some opposition to the Fifa president, with the efforts to force him out expected to intensify over the next few days.

On Tuesday Israel became the latest Fifa member to officially withdraw their support for Infantino’s re-election in a letter sent by the head of the Israel Football Association (IFA), Moshe Zuares.

The move is not a surprise as the IFA has been a member of Uefa since 1994 and Zuares sits on the European governing body’s executive committee, but it remains another blow to Infantino, who has invested significant political capital in attempting to improve sporting relations with Palestine.

At Fifa’s congress in April Infantino tried to stage a photo involving the two delegations in Vancouver, but the Palestinian Football Federation president, Jibril Rajoub, refused to stand alongside IFA ⁠vice-president, Basim Sheikh ⁠Suliman. Undeterred by this setback, Infantino wants Israel and Palestine to compete in the first match of a new under-15 tournament in the United States next month, as reported by the Guardian in June.

In his letter, which has been seen by the Guardian, Zuares says recent events have triggered an “unprecedented crisis of confidence” between the visions of Uefa and Fifa when it comes to global governance, adding that the rift is “profound, substantive, and principled, and compelling all stakeholders to reconsider the path forward”.

In a decision he described as being taken unanimously after a meeting of the IFA’s board, Zuares confirmed: “We have no choice but to retract our previous letter of support, in the sincere hope that fruitful dialogue among all parties will eventually restore a shared, proper vision and direction for world football.”

Israeli’s intervention echoes the withdrawal of support from other Uefa members including England, Wales, Scotland and the Republic of Ireland, and followed confirmation on Monday night that Lamour had left Fifa, having been deeply critical of Infantino’s Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal.

“If that means I lose my job, then so be it,” he said prophetically in a statement on 31 July. “I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.”

Another Uefa executive committee member, the former Wales Women international Laura McAllister, said the decision to sack Lamour “sends a deeply troubling message” and casts serious doubt over any efforts by the global governing body to recalibrate after the FFE scandal.

McAllister, who is one of five Uefa vice-presidents and worked there with Lamour before his move to Fifa in 2024, praised her former colleague for standing up to Infantino’s doomed scheme. “During the shabby events of the past weeks, he showed himself to be a courageous advocate for the most important stakeholders in football,” she said in a statement. “Kevin’s sacking seriously weakens Fifa’s administration, while undermining this unique opportunity to shift the culture at Fifa and to reset the organisation on sporting values, not simply commercial and financial ones.

“Fifa is not the president, it is the whole football family. As I have said repeatedly, world football needs strong, principled, independent leaders who are prepared to speak up, challenge when necessary, and stand firmly by their values and those of the global game. Instead, the loss of a leader of Kevin’s calibre sends a deeply troubling message to all of us seeking change.”

View image in fullscreen Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, said: ‘I don’t think Fifa should be ever contemplating selling off a stake in the World Cup.’ Photograph: Mike Egerton/PA

Meanwhile, Richard Masters, the Premier League chief executive, told the BBC that Infantino pressed the “self-destruct button” over his botched plan to bring private investment into the World Cup.

“This is a problem of Fifa’s making,” Masters said. “This is a self-inflicted wound. The organisation has pressed the self-destruct button, and the consequences of that flow now into the solutions that need to be found.

“I don’t think Fifa should be ever contemplating selling off a stake in the World Cup. They’re a not-for-profit organisation. They should really be holding that competition in trust for the future of football.”

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos consortium could be majority Liverpool shareholder within a year
Sports.content:
1892 Holdings, the new investor in Liverpool, has first refusal to become the majority shareholder in the next 12 months should Fenway Sports Group decide to sell.

The consortium led by Amit Bhatia and including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos was believed to have bought 30% to one-third of Liverpool when the deal was announced on Friday. However, the agreement is for 38% of the Anfield club, meaning 1892 has paid FSG just over £2bn to become a minority shareholder. The increased stake, first reported by the Athletic, still values Liverpool at about £5.5bn.

FSG also insisted on Friday the deal with 1892 was not part of an exit strategy from a club it bought for £300m in 2010 and it was not compelled to sell more of Liverpool to the consortium at a future date. That remains the case but should FSG decide to sell or reduce its shareholding in the next 12 months, then 1892 has an agreement in place that gives it the option to buy a controlling stake.

Liverpool’s majority owner has stressed it is an option for 1892 over the next 12 months, one that could lead to further investment, and is not a formal commitment on its part. FSG remains in operational control of Liverpool. But it does raise the possibility of Bezos, Bhatia and the Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, another billionaire member of the consortium, replacing FSG as Liverpool’s majority shareholders in the near future.

Bezos, one of the richest men in the world, is deemed a passive investor in Liverpool at this stage, having bought into 1892 through the K5 Sports fund, of which he is the lead investor. Bryan Baum, the co-founder and managing partner of K5 Global, will have a seat on an expanded Liverpool board alongside Bhatia as vice-chair and Elaine Saverin, wife of Eduardo. Bhatia has received financial backing from the Mittal Family Trust to buy into Liverpool. His father-in-law is the Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, another billionaire. The Mittal family are worth around $17bn and Saverin an estimated $33bn.

Sports.title: Pep’s final act of passion: Amazon’s revealing Guardiola series pulls no punches
Sports.content:
Having occupied a front-row seat for the final two seasons of Pep Guardiola’s gilded Manchester City tenure, the subject of Amazon’s A Beautiful Obsession, the surprise to me is how unfiltered the four-part series is.

Particularly, the telling of the torrid 2024-25 campaign when the wheels came clattering off in the bleakest of mid-winter plunges that featured nine defeats and one victory in 13 aura-shattering games.

To be shown from Wednesday on Prime, this series controlled and filmed by City is no hagiography of Guardiola or his players that seeks to paper over the great Catalan’s most harrowing season. Neither is the decision to let go of the club’s greatest modern-day player, Kevin De Bruyne, soft-soaped. And the anger of Khaldoon al-Mubarak, the chair, at Guardiola’s odd decision to change 10 players for last season’s 2-0 Champions League loss at home to Bayer Leverkusen is not left on the cutting-room floor.

Instead, the viewer witnesses up close and maybe too personal, when his divorce is cited as motivation, Guardiola flailing for solutions he fails to find. And shown, too, is how the ruthless business of football reduces a peerless manager and De Bruyne to the commodities they are, as City’s “machine built for winning” (Khaldoon’s description) must thresh on.

Guardiola talks about his marriage breaking down after a 2-0 defeat by Juventus in the Champions League on 11 December 2024. It was City’s seventh reverse in 10 games, so to try to rouse the team from their slump a disgusted Guardiola unloads about what went wrong between him and Cristina Serra.

View image in fullscreen Pep Guardiola bears cuts and scratches when facing questions in November 2024. Photograph: Amazon Prime

“I’m fucking divorced from the most beautiful woman on your planet,” he says. “I love her unbelievably, but we lost the passion. How do you play football, because you are paid? Or because of something inside? Where is the passion?”

This is an interesting choice. If Guardiola has every right to talk about personal issues, the decision seems counterproductive: a crossing of the professional/private line that could, conversely, make him appear weaker before his team, as normal managerial modes of motivation have lost their power. As he says later regarding what makes a good No 1: “You have to convince your players [that they would] go to the penthouse, the roof and jump down [for you].”

A year later, after the 10 changes against Leverkusen, Guardiola again says: “I leave my life, my divorce and my family is away, and everything for all of you. And what do you give back?”

Manuel Estiarte, in the second episode named The Rebuild, compounds the sense of a man running out of ideas when Guardiola’s close friend, and City’s director of first-team operations, reveals he told the players about the divorce, to let them know this is why “Pep is anxious, sad, different”.

Estiarte continues: “I said to the team: ‘Please, you have to understand, you’re not playing with a coach who can be a bit impulsive, intense, sometimes a bit up and down. You’re seeing a human being. He’s getting a divorce.’ It was necessary for the team not only to visualise Pep as a manager but for the first time as a human being.”

View image in fullscreen Guardiola’s decision to make 10 changes before a 2-0 defeat by Bayer Leverkusen led Manchester City’s chair Khaldoon al-Mubarak to say: ‘I can’t speak to him – I’m so angry.’ Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

First, you wonder why Guardiola did not impart this sensitive information himself to the players, as this might have aided the intended impact. Then, you ponder if Khaldoon and Ferran Soriano, City’s CEO, discussed whether the manager’s private life might be affecting his ability to do his job.

Interestingly, we cut next to a jovial Guardiola. “In my life I made a lot of changes – I got divorced and I have to settle a bit. But no complaints at all honestly,” he says before, tellingly, insisting he is a happy man – regarding his work. “In my job, yeah,” the manager says.

The theme of interpersonal relations is a leitmotif of the documentary – and so, by extension, Guardiola’s management style (episode three is titled: Love and Hugs).

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In “The Desert”, part one, he is close to tears after Kyle Walker abandons the teetering ship in January 2025, precisely when City need their captain. Walker did not behave like their leader, Guardiola tells the players, before a cutting rhetorical question: as they had voted him as the captain, why did they not pin him to the wall and demand more loyalty, he asks.

The scene that precipitates the defender’s departure is beautifully filmed and comes in the Anfield dressing room after Walker’s error leads to Luis Díaz winning a penalty converted by Mohamed Salah in the 2-0 loss.

Guardiola mentions this, causing Walker to fire back that the finger is being pointed at him “every meeting”. It ends with the manager in tears, delivering a soliloquy about how his signing of a new contract, only 11 days before, in the midst of the disastrous run, was because of a desire to fight. Juxtaposed in the shot, in a moment of cinematic panache, is Walker, now silently reflecting on his role in this. Guardiola says: “If captains first, then the other ones, for example [feel] that there’s a problem, tell me. It’s not going to change the love I have for all of you. I’m sorry.”

More regrets start episode two, after De Bruyne is not offered a new deal, and Soriano stresses to Khaldoon that “Kevin gets the respect he deserves as the greatest player in the modern history of City”. Guardiola reveals ‘Super Kev’ broke down in his office but also that there had to be coldness in the decision to offload him, before the Belgian is shown crying when asked what will be missed most. “My kids don’t want to go,” he says.

View image in fullscreen Guardiola hugs Kevin De Bruyne as the Belgian midfielder prepares to come on for his last appearance for Manchester City. Photograph: Dave Shopland/AP

Here, the viewer is reminded how those in elite sport can feel emotion, that tapping into passions is vital for success. And that beyond the game-face displayed on the pitch, and in front of the media and fans, are real relationships which bring joy – and hurt.

More admirable honesty is offered up when Guardiola’s 10 changes for that November 2025 defeat to Leverkusen are criticised. “Our attitude with Pep Guardiola should not be too negative. But it shouldn’t be too kind or accommodating either. This is his mistake this time,” says Soriano. To which Khaldoon says: “To pick an entire new [outfield] team in a game this important is probably one of the lowest points we’ve had. I can’t speak to him – I’m so angry.”

Yet, by the end of part four – “Nothing Is Eternal” – all seems comparatively rosy again. The Carabao Cup and FA Cup are claimed to make it 20 trophies (including three Community Shields) in a decade for Guardiola, and City finish second. With his rebuild done he receives a fitting send-off, before the start of the rest of his life. As he says: “Life should not just be about football. It’s too much to be honest.”

Sports.title: Barcelona steal Rodri away from Real Madrid and plan to make him new Busquets
Sports.content:
By the time Flight PTN27B started its descent into El Prat a bit before 8pm on Monday evening, a small crowd had gathered by the terminal doors, waiting for it to land. A few people stood and watched the sky, cameras out to capture its arrival. A lot more watched on their phones. In the two hours it had taken to get there from Manchester, taking off at 5.11pm, 101 minutes behind schedule, the Pilatus PC-24 had become the most tracked plane on the planet. Everyone knew that Rodrigo Hernández was on board. Unless, of course, he had been sneaked away in a catering cart.

Five days earlier, Rodri had been seen, and recorded, at Barajas airport waiting to get on a flight back to Manchester from Madrid. He wheeled a small RFEF (Spanish football federation) case with his name on, stood alone in the queue, the World Cup-winning captain just a bloke in shorts and T-shirt, and his stay in the UK was supposed to be brief, just long enough to say goodbye. The plane he was boarding was a Ryanair one: that was the detail everyone homed in on, something extraordinary in the ordinariness. This time, though, he came on a private jet, one way. His family travelled with him. He came to sign for FC Barcelona.

Rodri was late: an agreement between Manchester City and Barcelona had taken a little longer than expected, long enough for concern to creep in, and his flight landed 70 minutes behind schedule. Maybe he is late-late, too: at 30, and three years after the departure of Sergio Busquets – the man to whom he had always been likened and whose natural successor he has always been … this transfer could perhaps have come sooner. Yet it was rarely even contemplated, virtually up until the moment it happened. In that sense, it had actually been quick. A fortnight ago, few thought of this.

Now here he was, heading out in jeans and a white T-shirt. There was expectation, a hint still of disbelief that they had got him. A touch of relief, too, after the delay. They had been “intense days”, Rodri said, but now it was done. Barcelona’s third bid had been accepted: €60m plus a further €15m in add-ons, €11m of which are virtually guaranteed. He will earn around €15m a year, an increase on his salary at City, and has signed a four-year deal.

Quick Guide Rodri seals Barcelona transfer Show The Spain midfielder Rodri has completed his €60m move from Manchester City to Barcelona, signing a four-year contract after undergoing a medical on Tuesday. "Barcelona and Manchester City have reached an agreement for Rodri, who is committing to the Catalan club until 30 June 2030," read a club statement. Barça added that the 30-year-old is "considered one of the best players in the world in his position", and "stands out for his tactical intelligence, composure on the ball, ability to regain possession and precision in his passing". Rodri (pictured) was named the best player of the World Cup after Spain’s triumph this summer. He spent seven seasons at the Etihad Stadium, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the winner in the 2023 Champions League final against Inter. The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner joined from Atlético Madrid in July 2019, and was in the final year of his contract. In a message to City fans on the club’s website, Rodri wrote: "I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life but I am going to try. I knew I came into a top team but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made – winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect. "We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it," he added. "And the fans were with us every step of the way. City didn’t just make me grow as a player. They made me grow as a human ... Manchester shaped my whole life. It’s time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my teammates. This journey couldn’t be the same without you, my heart will always be blue." Barcelona saw an initial £40m offer and an increased bid turned down before an agreement was struck on Sunday. Rodri flew to Barcelona’s El Prat airport on Monday and told reporters: "Playing for Barcelona is a dream come true for me." The new City manager, Enzo Maresca, faces a race to rebuild his midfield, with Rodri joining Bernardo Silva in departing the club, Tijjani Reijnders poised to join Saudi Pro League side Al Qadsiah, and Newcastle reportedly interested in Nico González. Elliot Anderson has joined from Nottingham Forest for £116m and City have been linked with Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi and Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández. Photograph: Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Europe Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I’m happy to be here,” Rodri said, and they were happy to have him. The following morning he arrived at the club’s Joan Despí training ground to complete his medical, everything signed off. As he left the terminal building, Rodri had been asked if this was a dream come true. He of course said yes it was, which he had to say. The question had been direct, leading. It had been loaded too.

A Ballon d’Or winner and the embodiment of a style, an identity, that is theirs too, Rodri is the perfect fit. The time was right for him too. Voted the best player at the World Cup, the culmination of his recovery from injury, there was just one year left on his contract at City. He had won it all in England and Pep Guardiola had gone. After seven years away, home called. But home didn’t mean Barcelona; in fact, it had seemed more likely to mean Real Madrid.

View image in fullscreen Rodri lifts the World Cup after Spain’s victory over Argentina. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

Rodri grew up to the north-west of the capital and even Real’s refusal to turn up the night he won the Ballon d’Or, an act of grubbiness and disrespect, didn’t mean closing the door. Instead, he was increasingly open about his willingness – his apparent desire – to go. “Obviously, when the best club in history, the most successful with everything that brings, call you it is an honour and you always have to pay attention,” he said not long after the ceremony. In the spring, Rodri admitted he would like to return to Spain and that he would not rule out going to Real, even if he had been in the academy at Atlético. When Real held presidential elections in May, the pretender, Enrique Riquelme, announced that his signing would be Rodri. For his part, Rodri kept his counsel and come the end of the World Cup he had three offers: Paris Saint-Germain, who he ruled out because he wanted a return to Spain, Barcelona and Real.

Real, ambivalent before, appeared convinced by his status as the World Cup’s best player, president Florentino Pérez’s reticence seemingly overcome. He was exactly the footballer they needed, someone to get them to actually play, and Real were confident that he would come, that theirs was the only real offer. One headline summed it up: “Rodri is next”. This was done, which is when things tend to get undone. Rodri had an offer that was impossible to turn down. Only the terms of the negotiation shifted, doubts growing about Real’s commitment, frustration growing.

Barcelona, seeing an opportunity, pushed at an unexpectedly opening door. Rodri might not have been the player they needed most – a forward was their priority – but, well, he’s Rodri. This was undeniably a step up in quality, even for a midfield like theirs. Meanwhile, doubts over Frenkie de Jong’s fitness brought a reframing: maybe he was more necessary than they had believed. Likewise, that slight nagging doubt about his fit with Pedri in the selección feels like a small one, easily overcome, certainly no obstacle to bringing together arguably the best two midfielders in the world. Good luck getting the ball off them.

On the day that Real announced Vinícius Júnior had renewed his contract at the club and that they had made Yan Diomande the most expensive signing in their history, they also briefed that Rodri wasn’t coming after all. The excitement among fans at the Santiago Bernabéu turned to disappointment, a kind of lingering doom. That huge hole in the middle of Madrid’s midfield was still not plugged, their issues still not addressed.

View image in fullscreen Rodri enjoyed seven successful seasons at Manchester City. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

For Barcelona this was the signing of the summer. The World Cup winning-captain, perhaps the best player on the planet, was coming to Catalonia. There was a kind of gleeful disbelief, the expectation huge. Rodri thanked Madrid, but he had made his decision. As usual, Jorge Valdano put it best when the €75m deal had been done. “Rodri’s deal is worth €35m for what it gives Barcelona and €40m for what it takes away from Madrid,” he said. “At Real Madrid he would have revolutionised their play and improved everything.”

Valdano added he will not have the impact on Barcelona’s style that he would have had on Real’s, but that was because it is already his. “I always try to learn from Busquets,” said Rodri. “I watched him especially closely: he, and others, laid down a model of playing I knew I had to follow.” When Rodri joined City, Guardiola had found his other Busquets, or so it goes. Waiting patiently for his moment, when Busquets finally left the national team, it was always going to be Rodri who stepped in. A “perfect computer”, Luis de la Fuente called him. Doing so with Barcelona would seem natural, maybe even overdue, his signing a no-brainer.

Rodri’s World Cup overcame any doubts that it was too late, that his time had gone, and brought an extra dimension too, a shift in his role which he didn’t just embrace but consciously sought. He had the maturity, the leadership, the ascendancy over Spain’s young players – Barcelona’s young players – that they needed. And he needed too: there is something almost paternal about him and they had the youth that he wanted to lead, to guide. And, of course, the talent too. He knows how good it is to play with them: he had done so all summer, winning the ultimate award. And so it was done.

Now all that was needed was for City and Barcelona to reach an agreement. Eventually, they did, so Rodrigo Hernández had another plane to catch.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s boardroom rift: if Boehly goes who will Clearlake have left to blame? | Sam Cunningham
Sports.content:
Perhaps, in hindsight, it was always going to end this way. As some of the world’s wealthiest investors scrambled to find funds after Vladimir Putin’s invasion of Ukraine set a series of dominoes toppling that forced Roman Abramovich to sell Chelsea, it threw together some unexpected allies.

Todd Boehly became the public face of the winning bid, convincing the US sports mogul Mark Walter and the Swiss businessman Hansjörg Wyss to join as 12.8% minority investors. The private equity firm Clearlake Capital put in 61.6%, bringing the owners Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, who made their fortunes investing in tech, into the leadership fold.

But once the adrenaline rush of beating 11 serious rivals in an expedited bid process run by the Raine Group had worn off, that was really when the problems started. Now they actually owned Chelsea, how were they going to run it? What was the strategy? How would they tackle a stadium falling well behind their rivals?

Maybe Abramovich made running Chelsea look easier than it was. The club had not finished outside the top five for six seasons, yet in the four seasons since the takeover, their average league position is eighth – with a high of fourth and a low of 12th. Possibly the conflicting opinions of people who always think they are right, and have the money to prove it, is not the optimal setup.

Before the takeover, an agreement was struck that Boehly, representing Walter and Wyss, would have final signoff on major decisions alongside Eghbali and Feliciano. Over the years, Boehly and Eghbali have been the dominant day-to-day decision-makers at the club, while the others remained largely silent partners, insulated from the fan anger and social media ridicule that inevitably follows any period of struggle.

Some sources maintain that Boehly and Eghbali share a “professional” relationship, but signs of strain had leaked into the public domain long before this week’s revelation that Boehly and Walter were open to selling their stakes to Clearlake in a deal that would value the club at about £5bn.

In May 2024 Boehly told the Qatar Economic Forum that “patience” with the project was essential. Mauricio Pochettino had just led Chelsea to the EFL Cup final, the FA Cup semi-final and they had recovered from a poor start to finish sixth. Cole Palmer was a breakout star; Reece James was made captain. They won their last five games of the season.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso is aiming to rediscover the momentum Chelsea had built under Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Paul Dennis/TGS Photo/Shutterstock

Six days later, Pochettino was gone – dismissed after the co-sporting directors Paul Winstanley and Laurence Stewart compiled an 18-page review of the season.

Another glimpse of the pervading tension – and possibly a hint at what was to come – emerged in March last year in Boehly’s Bloomberg interview discussing the slow-moving stadium development plans, four years after they were announced.

“We have to think long term about what we’re trying to accomplish,” Boehly said. “We have a big stadium development opportunity that we have to flesh out. That’s going to be where we’re either aligned or we ultimately decide to go different ways.”

Publicly, Boehly insisted the ownership was aligned. Yet that is also at odds with how it began: the American installing himself as sporting director and driving a £250m spending spree targeting experienced players such as Raheem Sterling and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang. Chelsea finished 12th.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Boehly then stepped back, with Eghbali taking a more active role. About 70 interviews took place to build a new football structure, resulting in the appointments of Winstanley and Stewart – later promoted to co-sporting directors – and Joe Shields, now a co-director of recruitment.

They attempted to redefine how a football club is run: buying young, handing out unusually long contracts, in a model that has fascinated and baffled many in football. As an indication of how well that’s gone, in 2024 fans placed stickers around Stamford Bridge mocking up the three owners as clowns, while the Chelsea Supporters’ Trust described their club as “a laughing stock”.

The spending has been unprecedented – the pre-tax loss of £262.4m in the year ending June 2025 was a Premier League record supporters had probably not envisaged after Boehly declared the owners’ vision was “to make the fans proud” after the takeover. They have complied with Premier League spending restrictions only by effectively selling the women’s side to themselves. But it could not stop a significant fine for breaching Uefa’s financial rules, which did not permit the club to include the sale as income.

But there have been signs that the grand plan(s) will work. Momentum grew under Enzo Maresca Chelsea qualified for the Champions League and lifted the Club World Cup, and there was frustration that last season was derailed by his abrupt departure in January, after which they plummeted from Champions League contenders to 10th.

Now comes another reset under Xabi Alonso and a new strategy tweak towards older, more tried and tested players. But the boardroom drama persists. Both sides have explored buying each other out in recent years, but it appears Boehly’s and Walter’s hands have been forced. Walter, a long-term friend and business partner of Boehly, is under investigation by the US Department of Justice for alleged tax fraud and is believed to be selling assets to pay loans facing federal attention. He unexpectedly sold the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5bn (£9.2bn) last week and his Chelsea stake could be next.

An exit would coincide neatly with Boehly’s five-year tenure as Chelsea chair coming to an end at the conclusion of this season and a representative from Clearlake ready to fill his place. If a sale is agreed, Eghbali and Feliciano will have full control – and no one else to blame if things don’t improve.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala says ‘treatable seizures’ are reason for two collapses in four days
Sports.content:
The Bayern Munich winger Jamal Musiala has revealed he is suffering from “treatable absence seizures” after he collapsed on the pitch for the second time in four days.

Musiala fell to the floor eight minutes after coming on as a substitute in Bayern’s friendly with Heidenheim on Tuesday night. The 23-year-old experienced a similar incident during Saturday’s friendly against RB Leipzig, but Musiala has insisted there is no long-term health risk.

“First things first, I am doing well. I am incredibly grateful for your messages and your support!” Musiala posted on Instagram. “I understand that many of you are worried. I would like to put those concerns to rest today and explain the situation.

“I have been diagnosed with brief, temporary – but treatable – absence seizures resulting from a neurological dysfunction. These can lead to the kind of incidents seen recently, such as during the match against Leipzig or the game in Heidenheim.

“I know they might look alarming at first glance, but for me, they are currently part of my everyday life. I am receiving excellent medical care and remain very optimistic. FC Bayern and my personal support network are right by my side, helping me through this. Importantly, there is no further health risk involved.”

View image in fullscreen Jamal Musiala also had to leave the field during Bayern Munich’s friendly win over RB Leipzig on Saturday. Photograph: Midori Ikenouchi/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock

The Germany international added: “In close consultation and regular contact with the experts, it was my personal wish to face this challenge; with the medical clearance of the neurologists, I want to continue doing what helps my recovery most: simply living my life and pursuing my passion for playing football.”

Having come on for Ismael Saibari after 61 minutes against Heidenheim, Musiala was replaced by Cassiano Kiala eight minutes later. He appeared dazed as he received medical treatment and was helped off the pitch, with Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, moving to play down concerns soon after the game.

“Jamal will speak about this in the near future. We knew about it and we are aware of the situation,” Eberl said.

Bayern won the game 4-2, with Felipe Chávez, Arijon Ibrahimovic, Luis Díaz and Nathaniel Brown all on target. Musiala also required medical attention after collapsing in the match against RB Leipzig.

Sports.title: Transfer roundup: Dedic completes £29.5m Newcastle move, Wan-Bissaka loaned to Villa
Sports.content:
The chance to be reunited with Matthias Jaissle convinced Amar Dedic to swap Benfica for Newcastle in a £29.5m transfer. Dedic becomes Newcastle’s sixth signing of a turbulent summer on Tyneside and the 24-year-old Bosnia and Herzegovina international is likely to start at right‑back at home to Liverpool on Sunday.

“Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me,” said Dedic, who played for Newcastle’s new manager at RB Salzburg. “We know each other well; he knows what I can bring to the pitch and I’m really happy to play for him again. It’s a special feeling and a real honour to join Newcastle.”

With Tino Livramento still recovering from a calf injury, Newcastle’s lack of senior right-backs has been highlighted in pre-season and, soon after replacing Eddie Howe this month, Jaissle advised club executives that Dedic could fill the void. It helps that a defender also comfortable at left-back understands the German’s playing philosophy.

Newcastle are also talking to Manchester City about the possibility of signing the midfielder Nico González, having lost Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães.

Aston Villa have agreed a deal with West Ham to sign Aaron Wan-Bissaka on loan with an option to make his move permanent at the end of the season. Villa had an initial offer to take Wan-Bissaka on a straight loan rejected by West Ham. The Democratic Republic of the Congo defender will provide Unai Emery with cover for Matty Cash. Villa are also hoping to sign João Palhinha and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over the Portugal midfielder.

Brighton have signed the Canada forward Promise David from Union Saint-Gilloise on a season-long loan, with the move becoming permanent if certain conditions are met.

Juventus have signed Guglielmo Vicario from Tottenham on a season-long loan. The deal includes an option for Juve to make the goalkeeper’s move permanent at the end of ​the season, ‌Tottenham said. Vicario, ‌29, joined Spurs from Empoli ‌in 2023 and has made 117 appearances for the north London club. He was part of the side ‌that won the Europa League in 2025, ending the ​club’s 17-year wait for a major trophy, but lost his place to Antonin Kinsky after the arrival of Roberto De Zerbi as manager in March.

Sunderland were set to announce their acquisition of a new left-back after fending off competition from Roma and Newcastle to win the race to sign the Toulouse defender Dayann Methalie for £25.6m, but that transfer was on hold on Tuesday night after it emerged that the 20-year-old had failed part of his medical. Sunderland’s specialists are believed to have detected a potential back problem and the defender has now returned to Toulouse, where an independent French consultant is set to examine him.

A France Under-21s international, Metahlie made 28 Ligue One appearances last season and has been lined up to compete with Reinildo for a place in Régis Le Bris’s starting XI. Methalie, who had been about to sign a five-year contract at the Stadium of Light, is also comfortable operating as a left-sided central defender or wingback.

Harry Kane, meanwhile, has said “now is the time to start talking” about signing a new deal at Bayern Munich. The 33-year-old is entering the last season of his initial four-year deal at the Bundesliga champions.

Sports.title: Patrick Vieira appointed as head coach of Senegal, the country of his birth
Sports.content:
Senegal have appointed France’s 1998 World Cup winner Patrick Vieira as head coach, the country’s football federation announced, succeeding Pape Thiaw, who was dismissed in the wake of their World Cup exit.

The appointment of Vieira, who was born in Senegal, is a “strategic move”, the federation said in a social media post, aiming to “establish a high-level technical staff, in line with our country’s sporting ambitions”.

His main mission will be to revitalise the team after Senegal’s bruising loss to Belgium in the last 32 of the World Cup. Thiaw was sacked less than two weeks later. The 45-year-old former Senegal international had taken over in 2024.

The Senegalese football federation (FSF) president said at the time of his dismissal that toxicity had surrounded the team at the World Cup after Thiaw demanded a pay rise.

The Lions of Teranga had also suffered two defeats in the World Cup group stage, against France and Norway, before a 5-0 victory over Iraq secured their place in the knockout rounds.

View image in fullscreen Senegal led Belgium 2-0 in the 86th minute of their last-32 tie but after Youri Tielemans’ equaliser (pictured) he scored the winner in added time of extra time. Photograph: Alex Grimm/Getty Images

The appointment of Vieira, who grew up in France from the age of eight, was ratified on Monday, the FSF said. His official presentation would occur at a future, unspecified date, it added.

Vieira was a key part of a superb Arsenal side which won the English league three times between 1998 and 2004, before moving to Juventus and then Inter in Italy. After ending his playing career at Manchester City, Vieira cut his coaching teeth at New York City FC from 2016 before taking over the French top-flight side Nice from 2018 to 2020.

The 50-year-old returned to England as manager of Premier League side Crystal Palace in 2021 but was sacked in March 2023 after a 12-match winless run. He subsequently had short stints at Strasbourg and Italian side Genoa. He played 107 times for France and won the World Cup in 1998 as well as the Euros two years later.

Under Thiaw, Senegal won the Africa Cup of Nations final in January before being stripped of their title as a punishment for walking off the pitch during the chaotic final against Morocco. Senegal have appealed that decision, with a hearing to take place behind closed doors at the court of arbitration for sport in Lausanne, Switzerland on 8 October.

Sports.title: Newcastle working on deal for Man City midfielder Nico Gonzalez - as they race to secure Bruno Guimaraes replacement before opening clash with Liverpool
Sports.content:
Newcastle United have held exploratory talks with Manchester City over a potential deal for midfielder Nico Gonzalez.

The 24-year-old is one of a number of options Newcastle are considering to replace Bruno Guimaraes after his £75million move to Arsenal. They are keen to bring in an experienced midfielder to slot straight in before Sunday's Premier League opener at home to Liverpool.

Gonzalez had been open to a new challenge after failing to cement a regular starting place since making a £50m move from Porto in January 2025.

Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez is keen for first-team football and Newcastle are looking at a move

City remain keen to add Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille and Enzo Fernandez from Chelsea but have sold Rodri to Barcelona for £65m, as well as Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah for £52m. They are also open to similar offers for Gonzalez.

Enzo Maresca's side have signed Elliot Anderson and want to keep Mateo Kovacic but will be looking to secure more quality for their midfield.

Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, brought in earlier this month following the exit of Eddie Howe, insisted after Saturday's 2-1 friendly defeat at home by Bayer Leverkusen that his team will be ready for the new season.

‘We're not concerned (about Liverpool being so soon),' he said. 'We know the reality and we'll do the best out of the reality. But it’s a huge challenge. You’re all smart enough to see that. But what we can do, it's pretty simple – we can do our best every day together with the lads we have here.

‘The club knows exactly the needs (on transfers). We stick with the plan. There will be some changes, for sure.’

Sports.title: How Barcelona have pulled off the transfer of the summer by signing Rodri... despite fans in Spain being convinced he was set for bitter rivals Real Madrid
Sports.content:
How Barcelona have pulled off the transfer of the summer by signing Rodri... despite fans in Spain being convinced he was set for bitter rivals Real Madrid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It seemed for a very long time that the fairytale of the summer, the one about the king returning to his castle, would enter its final chapter within the walls of the Bernabeu Stadium.

That has been the narrative everyone has heard for at least the last year.

‘And after Diomande… Rodri ,’ read a headline in Spanish outlet Marca earlier this month. ‘At Real Madrid, there is great optimism regarding the arrival of the Spanish midfielder, the crowning achievement of a spectacular project spearheaded by Jose Mourinho,’ its author wrote.

A news article in a different Spanish publication, published more recently, was even more bombastic.

‘The City player has no doubts and is only considering one option. If he ends up leaving Manchester, there is only one possible destination for him: Real Madrid.’

And it makes sense that so many predicted that this would be the outcome. Why wouldn't the World Cup-winning Spain captain, who turned 30 in June and is desperate to leave England and return home, choose the bright lights of the world's biggest club?

Yet, after months of assumptions and increasingly confident reports, Rodri has chosen Barcelona instead. The decision has blindsided many in Spain, where a return to the capital had long been viewed as a near inevitability.

After months of assumptions and increasingly confident reports, Rodri has chosen Barcelona instead of Real Madrid

Why wouldn't the World Cup-winning Spain captain, who is desperate to leave England and return home, choose the bright lights of the world's biggest club?

After all, the Bernabeu is 20 miles from the midfielder's hometown of Villanueva de la Canada where, it seems, some of his family are still based. And what we do know is that the main reason Rodri wants to move home is because of family reasons.

Not only that, but it seems there are even some Real Madrid fans in Rodri's family. A dig back through the archives and it doesn't take long to stumble across a picture of one of his brothers in the famous white, blue and gold strip of Los Blancos. Despite Rodri having played for rivals Atletico Madrid in the past, the ties to the Madridistas are unavoidable.

Yet on Tuesday night, he sealed his £65.4m move to Barcelona - and insisted it was what he had always wanted. 'I’d like to say that I’m very happy to be here,' he said. 'It’s a very special day, a very important new chapter in my career. Barcelona is a fantastic club, a global benchmark for its approach to football and the values it represents. I had other options, but Barcelona was my first choice, and I made that clear.'

Rodri was all smiles during his unveiling as a Barcelona player on a deal to 2030 on Tuesday

While Real Madrid looked like the obvious destination from a distance, the more you examine Rodri's character and priorities, the easier it becomes to understand why Barcelona ultimately won out. Because if there's one thing most of us know about Rodri, it is that he doesn't want you to know very much about Rodri.

There is no Twitter feed or Instagram page or frankly any form of public persona. Nowhere to see where he has been on holiday or what, if any, his pets look like. No post-gym updates on how he is feeling after having back surgery at the end of July.

And crucially, nowhere to give insight into what Rodri has been thinking about his next destination, beyond the varnished, pre-meditated sentences presented to the media, which have been few and far between.

When asked whether his childhood at Atletico would be standing in the way of a move to Real Madrid, he left the door ajar: 'There are other players who've taken that path. Not directly, but over time. You can't turn down the best clubs in the world.'

But this was hardly Enzo Fernandez's conspicuous flirtation ('I really like Madrid'). It was a nod to the fact that, of course, he would entertain a conversation.

The rest of his close circle has been watertight too. The little you do find amounts to a brother’s LinkedIn page and his girlfriend Laura Iglesias’ private Instagram page, limited to just 500 followers. Love Island presenter Maya Jama, Ruben Dias' former girlfriend, is one of the few allowed access into Iglesias' secluded world.

Real Madrid is fame: glitz, glamour and Galacticos of Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Junior - while Barcelona is pure, unadulterated football

Seven of Rodri's World Cup-winning team-mates, five of whom joined him in the final, are set to become his club team-mates too

When you tot all of this up and look at what we do know about Rodri and his obsession with keeping his private life private, his feet on the floor and nurturing his self-professed ‘addiction’ to football, then Barcelona suddenly makes a lot more sense.

Real Madrid is fame: the glitz, glamour and Galacticos. Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Jude Bellingham. Barcelona, on the other hand, is pure, unadulterated football. Johan Cruyff and Pep Guardiola and Lionel Messi. Thinkers and artists who see football as an idea as much as the trophies in the cabinet.

A couple of years ago Rodri was told that his national team-mate Alvaro Morata said he would have won the Ballon d’Or sooner had he marketed himself better. His reply?

‘But I don’t play football for that. Maybe people would like me to be more marketable but I understand football differently. I know how it works so I don’t get frustrated if (I get overlooked). If one day someone wants to reward the work, that’s welcome, but it doesn’t bother me at all.’

At Barcelona, Guardiola’s disciple of tiki-taka and positional play will acclimatise perfectly, dictating tempo and using his flawless distribution and reading of the game in Hansi Flick’s well-oiled machine. Seven of his World Cup-winning team-mates, five of whom joined him in the final, are set to become his club team-mates too.

It wouldn't be unbelievable to think that Guardiola would have had a couple of words with his talisman about the perks of playing at the Nou Camp over the years. The great manager's departure from City last summer merely set the wheels in motion.

Rodri's age and price were an initial concern for Real Madrid president Florentino Perez, and while his performances at the World Cup had him convinced he should sign him, clearly not enough for City to snap their hand off at the offer.

Barcelona sporting director Deco caught wind that negotiations had failed to accelerate, and after deep-lying midfielder Frenkie de Jong returned from the World Cup injured, this was the moment to step in.

Barca's initial proposal was understood to be closer to £40million, below City’s valuation. But once Rodri informed Real Madrid that Barcelona was his choice, it merely became a matter of cutting a deal.

City will be pleased that they managed to get £65.4m for him, considering his age. After a difficult last season for the club in which he struggled in his return from an ACL injury, Rodri rebounded in dazzling style at the World Cup. If he is going to kick on into the new season, it remains to be seen for how long.

They still want an experienced player to come in after he goes, and that is even after they fork out around £80million for 18-year-old Ayyoub Bouaddi.

In a message to City fans on the club’s website upon leaving, Rodri wrote: 'I found that saying goodbye is one of the most difficult things in life, but I am going to try. I knew I came into a top team, but I never thought we could be able to create the legacy we made winning trophies, fans around the world, love and respect.

'We made an example to inspire the next generations not only because the success, also because the way we did it. And the fans were with us every step of the way.

'City didn’t just make me grow as a player. They made me grow as a human. I saw my brother graduating from Manchester Metropolitan University. I could see my girlfriend working for the NHS.

Rodri won four Premier League titles, the Champions League, two FA Cups and three League Cups in a glittering spell at City under Pep Guardiola

'Manchester shaped my whole life. It’s time to say goodbye, thanks to the club, the fans, the staff and my team-mates. This journey couldn’t be the same without you, my heart will always be blue.'

Now they must also adapt to what's next, and life without a man who has arguably been one of their most important ever signings. In just seven years his trophy cabinet boasts four Premier Leagues, three League Cups, two FA Cups, a Champions League, and a FIFA Club World Cup, if you'll count it.

Across his 298 matches, he has averaged 77 minutes per game, a figure which would be higher if it weren't for the careful management of his comeback following his return in 2025 from that knee injury. But more than that, he is a leader in the dressing room, and Maresca is already hinting at needing more experienced heads in to balance his young squad in his and Bernardo Silva and John Stones' absence.

Back in 2018, after Rodri had spent an impressive first season in La Liga with Villarreal, Barcelona, on the lookout for a Sergio Busquets successor, looked to sign him.

But Atletico Madrid wanted their increasingly impressive academy graduate back, and so Rodri moved back to the capital, and a year later he was Guardiola’s in rainy Manchester. Barcelona have no intention of making the same mistake again.

And, of course, plenty of Madridistas are now insisting they never wanted him anyway.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace land £11m American star, Sunderland's move for £25.7m new boy is in danger after medical... and Rodri sends emotional message to Man City fans: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa to reject Al Hilal's £38m Watkins bid

Aston Villa will reject Al Hilal's bid for striker Ollie Watkins. The Saudi club made an offer worth £38million for the England striker to test Villa's resolve.

Watkins, 30, is open to the move as the Saudi side have made a couple of proposals this summer but Villa want to keep him.

Tyjon wants out as Arsenal hover

Blackburn Rovers prospect Igor Tyjon has asked to leave amid ongoing interest from Arsenal. The 18-year-old forward has represented both England and Poland at youth level.

Ipswich's £18m bid rejected

Ipswich Town have had an offer of around £18m rejected by Bayer Leverkusen for Argentina midfielder Exequiel Palacios.

Exequiel Palacios featured for Argentina at the World Cup

Brighton bag Promise

Brighton have signed Canada striker Promise David, 25, from Belgian side Union Saint-Gilloise on a season's loan with obligation to buy for £22m.

American boy joins Palace

Crystal Palace have announced the arrival of Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake for £11million.

The 19-year-old American attacker joins on a five-year deal from the MLS side partly owned by Palace co-owner David Blitzer.

Gozo turned out 16 times in the MLS last season, scoring six goals and registering four assists.

His move to Palace was initially agreed over 10 days ago but was stalled by MLS paperwork. All MLS players are employed by the league, meaning transfers are centrally scrutinised and controlled.

Every deal must be approved by MLS, which assesses the terms before a transfer can be finalised, making delays commonplace.

Gozo will provide depth for Palace on the right wing, playing understudy to Ismaila Sarr. He becomes Palace’s sixth signing of the summer but just the second they have paid a fee for after Anan Khalaili joined from Union Saint-Gilloise.

Gozo said: 'I’m really looking forward to playing in the Premier League with Crystal Palace. It’s the dream of any footballer.'

BOBBY MANZI

Crystal Palace have signed American teenager Zavier Gozo from Real Salt Lake for £11million

One Hull of an offer for Garcia... as Tigers have talks over Forest's Bakwa

Hull City have offered around £4.5million for Real Betis forward Pablo Garcia as talks continue over a deal.

As Daily Mail Sport reported at the weekend, Hull turned to the highly-rated 20-year-old winger after talks for Leon Bailey fell through. Betis want at least £7m and a substantial sell-on.

Hull have also held talks with Nottingham Forest over a loan move for winger Dilane Bakwa. They have asked about Yeremay Hernandez at Deportivo Coruna and been offered Keito Nakamura from Reims.

They have also rekindled interest in Norwich right-back Kellen Fisher. The Tigers first made enquiries in July but Norwich have been reluctant to sell the 22-year-old.

Pablo Garcia in pre-season action against Arsenal earlier this month

Anfield youngster set for loan to Sheffield Wednesday

Liverpool winger Kieran Morrison is expected to finalise his loan switch to Sheffield Wednesday in the next 24 hours.

The 19-year-old Northern Ireland international has impressed during Liverpool's pre-season and has attracted varied interest from the likes of Wolfsburg and Bristol City.

Now League One Wednesday want to register the Northern Ireland international in time to face Bradford City in the Yorkshire derby on Thursday, with Liverpool keen to see him get regular game time in a competitive division.

Liverpool youngster Kieran Morrison, 19, is a prime target for Sheffield Wednesday

Morrison can play centrally in attacking midfield as well as wide. He joined Liverpool from Manchester United's academy and was called up to the Northern Irish senior squad for the first time, ahead of their World Cup qualifying play-off against Italy in March. He made his senior debut in June, playing the first half of a 1–0 friendly win over Guinea.

Liverpool are continuing negotiations for Paris St Germain winger Bradley Barcola but, as it stands, Liverpool are unlikely to pursue interest in his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye despite exploratory talks.

Villa agree Wan-Bissaka loan

Aston Villa have agreed a loan with option to buy for West Ham United defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Daily Mail Sport revealed last Wednesday that Villa were in pole position for the Congo international.

Villa were rebuffed in a cheeky attempt at a straight loan proposal but talks have since progressed for the 28-year-old to join Unai Emery's squad, with Villa's option to buy understood to be in the region of £18m.

Aaron Wan-Bissaka is set to swap West Ham for Aston Villa

Toon in talks with City over Gonzalez

Newcastle United have held exploratory talks with Manchester City over a potential deal for midfielder Nico Gonzalez.

The 24-year-old is one of a number of options Newcastle are considering to replace Bruno Guimaraes after his £75million move to Arsenal. They are keen to bring in an experienced midfielder to slot straight in before Sunday's Premier League opener at home to Liverpool.

For more on this story click HERE

Sunderland still pursuing speedy Catamo

Sunderland remain in talks with Sporting Lisbon winger Geny Catamo.

The pacy 25-year-old has 43 caps for Mozambique and is keen to make the move to the Premier League.

Negotiations are ongoing while Sunderland will also need to secure a work permit.

Rodri's emotional tribute to Man City after sealing Barca move

Barcelona have confirmed the signing of Rodri from Manchester City in a deal worth £65.4m.

The former Ballon d'Or winner, who helped City win four Premier League titles and a Champions League, has signed a four-year contract with the La Liga club and will wear number 16.

Rodri, 30, had one year left on his City contract and, while they wanted him to stay and sign an extension, Barcelona's final offer proved too good to turn down.

Enzo Maresca's side are pursuing replacements for both Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders, who is set to join Saudi Arabian side Al Qadsiah for around £52m.

Lille's Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez of Chelsea are their targets.

And Rodri paid an emotional tribute to his now former club, saying: 'It’s not like I miss [City] because I don’t feel like I’m leaving. I think I’m just moving to another club, but my heart will always be linked to the city and to the club.

'I always try to be involved in the games, try to come and watch them and keep in touch with my ex-teammates. But of course, physically you leave. Seven years is the right moment to say goodbye, to write a good story.

'I always say that the most important thing is to have the whole image, the whole movie, and say I’m proud of this.

'Both parts, club and player, we’re proud of this, and this was the reason for my decision. My heart will always be blue all my life. And they always have Rodri for anything they need.'

Rodri was in demand and has now signed a four-year deal at Barcelona

Sunderland's Methalie move at risk

Sunderland's move for Toulouse defender Dayann Methalie is in danger of collapse after concerns were raised over his medical.

The 20-year-old is returning to France with further testing required.

Methalie underwent his medical yesterday after visiting the Stadium of Light.

Sunderland agreed a £25.7m deal on Sunday for the France Under 21 international left-back.

Dayann Methalie (centre) was set for the Stadium of Light but his move is now up in the air

Sociedad want West Ham's Edson

Real Sociedad have followed up their interest in West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez.

The Mexico international also had interest from former club Ajax but is keen to move to La Liga and talks are ongoing.

Stoke want to seal deal for Hirst

Stoke City have revived talks for Ipswich Town striker George Hirst in the hope of signing him by the weekend. Stoke travel to Southampton on Saturday.

Betis progress on Parrott after West Ham bid rejected

Real Betis are making progress in talks with AZ Alkmaar over a deal for striker Troy Parrott.

West Ham had an initial £15m bid rejected and were expected to go back but talks with Alkmaar have proved difficult.

The Hammers have since moved to finalise a loan for Leeds striker Joel Piroe.

Betis could be helped in their pursuit of Parrott by Hull's interest in their winger Pablo Garcia whom is valued around £7m.

Boro cancel Dieng's contract

Middlesbrough goalkeeper Seny Dieng has had his contract terminated by mutual consent. Dieng saw a loan move to Feyenoord fall through in January.

The 31-year-old has now linked up with Greek side Atromitos.

Vicario joins Juventus on loan

Tottenham have confirmed that goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario has joined Juventus on an initial loan.

The deal includes an option to buy for £8.5m (€10m).

The 29-year-old travelled to Turin yesterday after talks accelerated on Sunday once Juventus opted against signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa.

Tottenham goalkeeper Vicario has joined Juventus on loan

West Ham finalise move for Piroe

West Ham are finalising forward Joel Piroe's arrival from Leeds United as misfit striker Niclas Fullkrug joins Werder Bremen on a season's loan.

The 33-year-old Germany international, who joined the Hammers for £27m from Borussia Dortmund in August 2024, scored three goals in 11 Premier League starts but spent the second half of last season on loan at AC Milan.

Fullkrug, a German international, returns to Werder for a third spell having also started his career with the Bundesliga club.

Toffees chief pleads calm on right-back search

Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear is confident the club will sign a right-back but admits it will not be completed before the season opener against Crystal Palace on Saturday.

Speaking to BBC Radio Merseyside, Kinnear said: 'I don’t think we are in a bad position on that.

'The players we thought we had the option of are still available for us, I don’t think they will be there for Crystal Palace, which was the objective.

'I’m confident that we’ll bring a right back in. It’s a position we’ve needed. I think Jake (O’Brien) has done a sterling job for us in that position.

'It was something that we were trying to do last summer and didn’t feel that we could get the quality in.

'So a right-back was top priority in the window, we would have liked to have got it done earlier.

'I understand the fans' frustrations; I understand how they see it as being critical.

'Even the Prime Minister chipped in to give us some helpful direction. So it’s reached a level of national importance.

'So we are working hard to bring one in and I’m sure we will. I’m sure it will be an improvement, and it will round off the squad nicely.'

Everton have looked at Palace's Daniel Munoz though Moyes regards him more as a wing-back. They enquired about Fulham's Timothy Castagne and had a bid rejected for Celtic's Alistair Johnston who picked up an injury.

Others such as Guela Doue at Strasbourg are considered too expensive while they have been offered Aston Villa target Aaron Wan-Bissaka but said no and, similarly, are not pursuing Burnley's Kyle Walker, so far.

Moyes has admitted they may have to revert to another option if they can't get their prime target.

Newcastle complete Dedic deal

Newcastle United have signed Bosnia and Herzegovina international Amar Dedic from Benfica for £29.5million on a five-year deal.

The 24-year-old full-back becomes the sixth senior addition of the summer and will wear the No 37 shirt at St James' Park.

Dedic, who can operate on either flank, previously worked with Newcastle head coach Matthias Jaissle at Red Bull Salzburg and Liefering.

He made 95 appearances for Salzburg before spells with Marseille and Benfica, where he featured against Newcastle in last season's Champions League.

Newcastle United have completed the signing of full back Amar Dedic

Dedic has won 31 caps for Bosnia and Herzegovina and played at this summer's World Cup.

'Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well. He knows what I can bring on the pitch and I'm really happy to be playing for him again,' he said.

'Playing Premier League football at St James' Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I'm really excited to get started.'

Fulham monitor Brazilian defender Natan

Fulham have asked about Real Betis centre back Natan.

The Brazilian joined Betis from Napoli last summer for £7.5m and has attracted interest from other Premier League sides in recent weeks.

The 25-year-old is one of a number of options being considered by the Cottagers. They retain interest in Rennes defender Abdelhamid Ait Boudlal, too.

And elsewhere...

Aston Villa have agreed to loan right-back Kosta Nedeljkovic to Rangers with an obligation to buy for £3.5m.

Celtic also hold an interest in the Serbian international but he is expected for a medical at Ibrox later today.

Wolves are exploring a move for Brighton winger Amario Cozier-Duberry. Rangers had a £7.5m bid rejected this week for the £10m-rated 21-year-old.

Brighton have been exploring a move for Millwall forward Femi Azeez.

Sports.title: Aston Villa to REJECT Al Hilal's £38million bid for England striker Ollie Watkins
Sports.content:
Aston Villa to REJECT Al Hilal's £38million bid for England striker Ollie Watkins

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Aston Villa will reject Al Hilal's bid for striker Ollie Watkins.

The Saudi club made an offer worth £38million for the England striker to test Villa's resolve.

Watkins, 30, is open to the move as the Saudi side have made a couple of proposals this summer but Villa want to keep him.

He scored 16 Premier League goals last season - matching his tally from the previous campaign - while only Erling Haaland and Mo Salah have managed more than his 77 across the last five seasons.

Watkins did not travel to Salzburg for the Super Cup clash with Paris Saint-Germain last week as part of the club's plans for their players who went deep into the World Cup, but as it stands the club are planning for him to be available for their Premier League opener at Brighton this Sunday.

Ollie Watkins has been prolific for Aston Villa since joining from Brentford in 2020

Villa have been looking at a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson this summer, as previously reported by Daily Mail Sport.

Villa, meanwhile, have agreed a loan with an obligation to buy West Ham defender Aaron Wan-Bissaka. The fee is understood to be around £18m and he will have a medical on Wednesday.
